# The owner's four questions about propagation and consolidation, and what was found (collated for adjudication)

_Source: the owner's messages in the session `session_2026-11-16-remediation-batch-1-tooling-stack`, and the coordinator's answers, each checked against the repository on 2026-11-17 where stated. Derive every count; none is typed to be trusted. A claim marked [UNVERIFIED] was not confirmed in code._

## The owner's questions, verbatim

**Q1.** "how does this pipeline handle identifying new topics for research, conducting them in another language, verifying a source is reputable, adjudicating how much of the source is relevant across different topics, writing down everything relevant including new topics if they don't already exist, judging the parameters for their values as well as assigning their codes as well as assigning evidence tier as well as determining category, and then synthesizing everything within the topic so that it can form a specification/determination?"

**Q2.** "is there an iterative loop with limited repetitions to ensure exit such that you can ensure that topics across languages and synonyms are properly consolidated and associated in base with those consolidations propagating forward throughout database so we don't end up with duplicates or near identical topics?"

**Q3.** "you have identified missing items. what else exists in pipeline that allows us to work in all directions and systematically perform new passes over already-recorsed rows to ensure that the database codes/terms/etc are consistently applied as well as to append existing rows with more information as required if the base gets extended?"

**Q4.** "in fact, how does the pipeline handle propagation in all directions whenever there is a change made to a row or a new row somewhere is made?"

**The instruction that asked for this file:** "have Opus collate all of my questions about this and all of your answers/findings then adjudicate best fixes before planning out how to build followed by folding it into remediation plan".

## What the pipeline does today (checked)

**Q1 (flow).** Seven stages (`governance/pipeline-contract.yaml`, `stages:`): base, research, evidence, judgment, synthesis, specification, render, with ruled backward edges (T-022 writes them into the contract, on the stacked branch). Topics are `slugs`, authored from the ICF/access-need frame, never from the retired item list (DR-2026-08-19 section 1.4). A new concept enters as `observe-term` (verbatim, unjudged), is settled by `adjudicate-term` (outcomes NAMES-NEW, NAMES-EXISTING, DEFERRED, NOT-OURS), then `add-term` / `add-parameter` (needs a quantity kind and a warranting observation since T-020, stacked branch) or `decline-parameter`. Language: a search carries language and jurisdiction; coverage is per parameter and bucket member (`lang_jur_map`); no back-translation (R11); translations have a typed table (T-049, stacked branch), shown only when reviewed (the reader gate is T-037, not built). Reputable: no flag; verification (R10 re-retrieval, logged retrieval manifest, author fidelity check) plus tier computed from evidence type and scope (`derive_tier`, checked by `adjudication_integrity`); type and scope are judged. Relevance across topics: R16, every admission read against the whole parameter list (`record-scan`, `source_scans`); relevance is extraction rows per parameter, not a source score. Values: `source_value_extractions`. Codes: identity, ICF and access-need columns on the extraction and `extraction_lens_links`, written by judgment (the maps only propose); three lenses since the medical lens was deleted on 2026-11-16. "Category": not verified as one field. Synthesis: `convergence_assessment`, Opus-only; determination: `specifications` keyed on parameter plus at least one lens column, computed by the engine (`pilot-7`), not hand-assigned.

**Q2 (consolidation).** There is NO iterative, bounded consolidation loop. What exists: a write-time near-duplicate refusal (`db.py _near_terms`: token-set subset or superset against every canonical name and every alias not `model_seed`, in any language; refused unless `--distinct-from TERM-ID` with a rationale); adjudication NAMES-EXISTING; `merge-parameter` (re-points every foreign key into the folded parameter, table list read from the live schema; refuses a live determination or open gate), `rename-term`, `retire-parameter`. Bounded iteration exists only for citation mining depth and a recorded `saturation_signal` on searches.

**Q3 (passes over recorded rows).** Owed work is DERIVED, not executed: `v_scan_ledger` (one row per unsuperseded source and active parameter; status EXTRACTED, STATED-ABSENT, READ-NOTHING-FOUND, BLOCKED, or not read / partly read), `v_reading_owed`, the advisory `scan_debt` (no baseline by design, red whenever debt > 0), `v_deferred_acts` (a deferral stands while its cell is owed), `v_coverage_priority` and the other `v_coverage_*` views, `unmined`, `unmined-gaps`, `cell-status`, `coverage`. Adding to a recorded figure is by new pointer rows (`add-lens-link`, `retire-lens-link`, `add-population-icf-link`, `retire-identity` with a successor), retire-in-place (specifications; admission edges and connections once T-050 merges), and narrow `amend-*` verbs (`amend-extraction` is reformat-only). Read-only audits: `column_vocabulary_audit`, `schema_reference_audit`, `identifier_floor_audit`, `alias_provenance_audit`, `adjudication_integrity`, `extraction_relations_integrity`, `derivation_handshake_integrity`, `derived_not_curated_audit`, `graph_audit`, `test_db_integrity`, `migration_reproducibility`.

**Q4 (propagation).** By pull and by refusal, not push. The schema has ONE trigger (`trg_spec_retire_needs_reason`). A change reaches others because they point at the row (rule 5; 29 views), through cascades in one place (`merge-parameter`, successors, `merged_into` followed by `v_deferred_acts`), through writers that refuse until dependents are handled (merge/retire refuse live determinations and open gates), through determinations as recomputable caches (`derivation_sha` hashes the graded link set and each figure's in-lens state and the three lens codes; `derivation_handshake_integrity` recomputes), through the capture path (scratch copy, `dbcore.writable_tables`, `emit_batch_sql`, migration only) and replay checks, and through read-only audits.

## The gaps identified (G-numbers are this file's, for the adjudication to cite)

- **G1.** No bounded, exit-guaranteed consolidation sweep for topics/terms/synonyms across languages.
- **G2.** No `merge-term` verb (only `merge-parameter`, `rename-term`, `retire-parameter`) [UNVERIFIED: the verb list was read by name, not every parser].
- **G3.** No cross-language concept identity: a concept is keyed on an English string. Tasks that address it and were open when the plan was generated: T-028 (concept identity, NOT FOR SONNET), T-029 (typed pointers between terms), T-057 (base coverage view), T-069 (promote adjudicated non-English observations to forms); T-028-design.md exists.
- **G4.** The near-match gate skips `model_seed` aliases; live aliases are all `model_seed` or `unrecorded` (derive: `select attestation, count(*) from term_aliases group by 1`), none attested, so a cross-language near-duplicate is caught only through an unrecorded alias.
- **G5.** Owed passes are listed, not executed: no scheduler, no bounded re-pass, no exit rule; `scan_debt` and `verified_scan_integrity` are red today.
- **G6.** Re-assigning lens codes to old figures when the base grows is a judgment; the writer's proposals (T-126) are unbuilt; OD-67 (the population-to-ICF rows) was referred back to the owner.
- **G7.** Propagation is detected by audit, not on write; several audits are advisory; migrations, the verification cron and unknown routes bypass writer refusals.
- **G8.** `derivation_sha` does not hash a source's verification and tier, a row's grading and comparator, or a `confirms` edge (stated in `scripts/audit/derivation_handshake_integrity.py`); a stored determination can be stale without the sha moving.
- **G9.** Tolerated second homes: `specifications.functional_basis` (a JSON snapshot) and a gate's `trigger_tier`.
- **G10.** Prose callers and generated files are not swept by a gate (CLAUDE.md rule 4; `context_map_fresh` covers the context map only).
- **G11.** `python3 workplan/pipeline-state-graph/build_graph.py --check` reports about a hundred failures on the base, unchanged by each task of the stacked branch; `gaps` is `cross-stage` in the stage map but `walkability.py` leaves a cross-stage table outside the spine (OD-11 "count it as a member of each stage it carries" is not met).
- **G12.** "Category" in Q1 is ambiguous: evidence type, claim type, a term's `domain`, quantity kind or `design_scale`; the owner was asked which and has not said.
- **G13.** Task-level findings of the stacked branch that are the owner's or a design question are in `scratchpad/session_2026-11-16-remediation-batch-1-tooling-stack/sweep-list.md` (one section per task: T-020, T-022, T-049, T-050, T-089 once written, and T-093). Several bear on propagation: the translation view cannot hide a stale translation (no hash in SQL; T-037 must check), `retirement_reason` has no reader, readers of `connections` and `search_admissions` needed filters added by hand, the graph extractor ignores `re_entry`.
- **G14.** DR-2026-08-19 section 12.5 lists "tier and evidence-type assignment" as permanently manual; CLAUDE.md rule 8 derives the tier from type and scope. The reconciliation (type and scope judged, tier computed) was stated, not recorded in a ruling.

## What the stacked branch has already built toward this (for the adjudication to build on, not repeat)

T-020 (quantity kind and warrant on a parameter), T-022 (re-entry edges in the contract and `pipeline_contract_audit`), T-049 (`translations` and `v_translations_current`, `translation_pointer_audit`), T-050 (retire-in-place for admission edges and connections), T-089 (`refusal_register.py register` and `classes`). Each carries a repair commit after an adversarial pass. The first four are on the branch `ccr-cc893571-i4lug4`; derive the state with `git log --oneline origin/main..HEAD`.

# Sweep list: what the critics found and did not repair, and why (owner instruction 2026-11-15, "sweep … forward and backward")

Derive every count; none is typed here. One section per task; a finding is repaired in the commit named, or is the owner's / a design question with the file that would change.

## T-020 (commit d1bfc280; critic repairs in the next commit on the branch)

Repaired in the repair commit: order of the new refusals now held by T020-09 (red when the kind block is moved ahead of the earlier refusals); T020-08 splits the id-shape probes so each rule fails alone and re-reads the refusal to see the fixture kind listed (red when the id pattern admits a digit); `insert_parameter` refuses a non-string `--quantity-kind` instead of raising AttributeError; the skill sentence that counted the verbs taking `--approval-ref` now derives them by a grep.

Not repaired:
1. **The warrant's digit test admits a quote whose only digit is not a value** (a year, a clause number, "Class 1"). It conforms to T-020 section 4 item 1a(iii) as written; section 3 promises "an observation of a source stating a value of the quantity". Tightening it (a digit adjacent to a unit, or an adjudicated extraction) would add what section 4 does not name. A design question for the file `tasks/T-020-quantity-kind.md` (section 4, 1a(iii)) and for T-109, which assigns the live parameters their kind. Today the warrant is recorded and contestable, not proven.
2. **`insert_parameter` records the judgment under a blank session** (`session='  '`). Pre-existing (not a weakening); `insert_quantity_kind` refuses it. A small refusal in `insert_parameter` would close it; it is not named by T-020, so it is left for a task that names it.
3. **Migration 143 line 2 types "six-kind seed"** (rule 7a). The migration is committed and immutable (rule 3); the sentence is a comment and cannot be edited. The commit message of d1bfc280 carries two typed counts for the same reason and is history.
4. **`STATE-GRAPH.md` and `graph.json` lack T-020's guard and `add-quantity-kind`.** They are generated; regenerated in the end-of-batch sweep (owner instruction 2026-11-15, item 4), not per task.

## T-022 (commit 1ca23587; critic repairs in the commit after it)

Repaired: both B12 edges removed (the owner's statement of 2026-11-06 (seventh) supersedes the route for base vocabulary: rule 0; the executor had entered them on its own reading, which the task file did not state); the B11 edges no longer say "until the owner answers OD-10" (answered 2026-11-12) and now state what the carrier selects (every skim, not only a skim under a determination); the B7 edge no longer claims "T1-T2" (the carrier is any mined source); the audit refuses an edge id held twice (T022-09); T022-10 holds the stage EARLIER than the carrying stage (the `<=` to `==` mutant now fails); `test_pipeline_contract` fails when no return is ruled at all (deleting every `re_entry` block no longer passes). Each guard was run red on a seeded defect and the file restored byte for byte. The task file carries both corrections.

Not repaired (a design or owner question, or data):
1. **Three of the six carriers carry nothing today** (derive: `gaps.parameter_id` populated rows, `term_aliases.source_url` populated rows, `extraction_follow_ups` rows). The audit holds that a carrier exists and its value is in the column's CHECK, not that it is used; "never used" is a fact of the data, which later research fills.
2. **B10 cannot name "open" as a carrier value**: `gaps.status` is a LIKE check, so `dbcore.check_values` returns no set. The edge names the column only. A real CHECK on `gaps.status` would be a schema change this task does not name.
3. **B13 names `source_url` only**; the boundary table says URL, page and line. `term_aliases` also has `source_page` and `source_line`; a second carrier per edge is not what the schema of `ReEntry` allows, and the owner's statement says page and line are "if need be".
4. **B11 and the two skim edges share one carrier**, so the edge cannot tell an evidence-origin return from a judgment-origin one. They are two edges because the boundary table has two re-entry stages; whether a single edge with two target stages is better is a design question for `governance/pipeline-contract.yaml`.
5. **The graph ingest ignores `re_entry`** (`scripts/audit/graph/extract_contract.py` renders stages and criteria only), so the ruled returns are absent from the state graph. A later task that renders them owns it; the end-of-batch sweep regenerates the derived files.
6. **B9 and B14 are not entered**: the boundary table marks them "ledger" and "inferred", not "ruled".

## T-049 (commit 3818ed33; critic repairs in the commit after it)

Stopped once: the executor's section 3 flag `--source-row-key` ended in a secret word (`key`), and `dbcore._secret_flag` redacts such a flag's value in the refusal recorder (T-088, case T088-05b). Renamed the FLAG to `--source-row-id` (the column stays `source_row_key`); exempting it would weaken a T-088 guard. The task file records the rename.

Repaired: the definition of "current" had three homes (the view, `_current_translation`, the audit); the verbs and the audit now read `v_translations_current`; four refusals no test held now have a case each, each run red on a seeded defect (T049-87 own-language request, T049-88 blank session, T049-89 unknown target language, T049-90 translator kind outside the CHECK, which names the kinds the CHECK holds); T-037's task file now states that the renderer must hash-check a translation before showing it.

Not repaired (the spec's own wording, a design or owner question):
1. **OD-30 is recorded, not enforced, at the read surface.** The view admits `translated` rows (T-049 item 2) and the reader gate is T-037's (item 8). The commit message of 3818ed33 says the registry entries check that no translation is shown unreviewed; they check pointer, hash and numbers. The claim is history; this note corrects it.
2. **The reviewer check is a case-insensitive name compare** (item 8). A near-identical name, the same session and a non-Opus model all pass; the database cannot verify a model class. Whether the review's session must differ from the translator's is a rule the file does not state (task file, design question (b)).
3. **A translation equal to its original is accepted**: no flag carries the original, but the text a translator supplies is not compared with it (design question (c)).
4. **The number rule refuses `1 200 mm` to `1,200 mm`, and passes a reordered pair, a changed unit and a flipped comparator** (item 5; design question (a)). A change to item 5 and T-008's reader.
5. **A stale translation stays in the view** after its original changes; the verbs refuse it and the advisory audit reports it, and T-037 must check the hash (now stated in its file). A stale `requested` row has no verb that closes it.
6. **The joined-cells census examines no translation column** while the table holds no row (it counts columns with data). Re-run it after the first translation is written.
7. **`translations` rows and other tables' keys are translatable cells** (`translations.translated_text`, `evidence_sources.ref_id`): the file lists no translatable tables, by design.

## T-050 (commit 77f86902; critic repairs in the commit after it)

Repaired: `add-connection`'s duplicate check read retired connections as live, so a withdrawn relationship could never be recorded again (it filters now; T050-08); `update-connection` wrote to a retired connection (it refuses and names `add-connection`; T050-09); the missing-id refusals said `db.py connections` lists "the ids that exist", false for retired ids (they say live ids); `skills/connection-discovery_SKILL.md` Step 0 told the session to hand-join `connection_targets` unfiltered (it now keeps `retired_at IS NULL`, and says a retired connection does not block a duplicate). Tests that held none of these filters, each run red on a seeded defect: T050-07 (cell-status), T050-08, T050-09, T050-10 (link-admission counts live edges; the unlink side was held by U03).

Not repaired:

# Remediation workplan: a pipeline that runs in every direction, at any stage, across languages and jurisdictions

_Written 2026-11-12 (UTC) by the handshake-and-adversarial leg of the bidirectional-pipeline audit. Planning only: no script, schema, governance file or database row was changed in writing it. Canadian English. Every figure is given as the command that produces it; re-run the command, do not trust a number._

## Precedence (2026-11-14): the term-resolution plan over this plan; the ledger over both

**The owner instructed on 2026-11-14** that the term-resolution plan be folded into this plan, "with this newest plan having priority in conflicts" (ledger: `grep -n -F "Owner instruction 2026-11-14 (last) — fold the term-resolution plan" references/project-standards.md`). So: where this plan, its task files, `OPEN-ITEMS-PLAN.md`, `DECISION-CLOSURE.md` or `OWNER-SHEET-PLAIN.md` disagree with [`TERM-RESOLUTION-PLAN.md`](TERM-RESOLUTION-PLAN.md) (best, ideal and most accommodating as one quantity; most common practice; the minimum; the four figures; showing and grading; the markers and ⚠; stage names), **the term-resolution plan governs**, and the passage changed to match carries a note "Superseded in part by TERM-RESOLUTION-PLAN section n (2026-11-14)". Where either plan disagrees with an owner ruling in the ledger (`references/project-standards.md`), **the ledger governs** (CLAUDE.md rule 0). The fold, item by item, and every conflict it resolved with the text before and after: [`TERM-PLAN-FOLD.md`](TERM-PLAN-FOLD.md). The term plan's tasks are T-117 to T-121 and additions to T-035, T-059 and T-068; its open questions are OD-57 to OD-62.

## 0. Verdict

**Since this was written (2026-11-12, later the same day).** Twenty of the owner decisions were delegated to an Opus-class model, and the owner's twelfth instruction asked that the remaining ones be confirmed and, where appropriate, resolved before the plan is called complete. Which decisions stand, which hold up a task and which are answered is read from the ledger, never from this sentence: run the gate loop of section 13, or regenerate `REMEDIATION-PLAN.md` (its owner decision queue splits them into blocking, standing and open). Section 13 records the delegated pass and the gate; `DECISION-CLOSURE.md` records the twelfth-instruction pass, the decision-by-decision confirmation and a phone-ready prompt for every decision still the owner's.

**The owner's objective is not met today, and it can be met.** The objective (`grep -n -F "run in all directions" references/project-standards.md`): the pipeline "can be run in all directions at any stage in such a manner where we can dynamically research, adjudicate, synthesize, specify and render across a multitude of languages and jurisdictions". Three later statements of the same day add that the code be "efficient and centralized and clean", that the pipeline be flexible, glossed by the owner as having no "hard coded behaviours", and that it have no dead ends (`grep -n -E "^## Owner statement 2026-11-12" references/project-standards.md`).

What stands in the way, in order of harm to the book:

1. **A determination is computed without regard to the group it is for.** The engine gathers evidence by parameter alone. Fixed by the chain [T-016](tasks/T-016-wp-t1a-reading.md) → [T-017](tasks/T-017-wp-t2-conditions.md) → [T-018](tasks/T-018-link-table.md) → [T-019](tasks/T-019-lens-gather.md).
2. **Guards that a wrong figure or a misquote should not pass, pass it**: the number check (a figure written in words is now entered as a numeral, by the owner's ruling of 2026-11-12), the quote and name checks outside Latin script, a source admitted with no verification standing. [T-008](tasks/T-008-claimed-number-check.md), [T-009](tasks/T-009-script-aware-guards.md), [T-007](tasks/T-007-add-source-standing.md).
3. **The mobility group the owner decomposed by device is still one code**, and most figures sit on it. [T-055](tasks/T-055-mobility-family-tooling.md), [T-102](tasks/T-102-mobility-split.md) (OD-14 and OD-31 answered 2026-11-12).
4. **Nothing exists at render**, so every stage pair ending there has no path. [T-037](tasks/T-037-render.md), [T-038](tasks/T-038-stage-pair-gate.md) (its decisions resolved under delegation; OD-04, which held it through T-101 and T-036, answered by the owner on 2026-11-12).
5. **The base is English-shaped and its scope is in no table**: jurisdictions in code, scope unrecorded, forms unattested. [T-024](tasks/T-024-jurisdiction-registry.md), [T-025](tasks/T-025-base-writers.md), [T-026](tasks/T-026-alias-attestation.md), [T-101](tasks/T-101-scope-fill.md), [T-028](tasks/T-028-concept-identity.md).
6. **A step backward leaves no typed cause**: a gap does not say what it is a gap in. [T-013](tasks/T-013-typed-gaps.md), [T-012](tasks/T-012-follow-up-reasons.md), [T-022](tasks/T-022-contract-re-entry.md).
7. **A source must be re-read for every later parameter, parameters are flat, and synthesis finds nothing.** [T-031](tasks/T-031-clause-unit-and-open-pass.md), [T-029](tasks/T-029-term-relations.md), [T-032](tasks/T-032-synthesis-relations.md), [T-033](tasks/T-033-synthesis-candidates.md) (OD-23 answered by the owner: a clause inventory backed by retained text, a flagged re-read where neither reaches; the others' decisions are resolved under delegation).
8. **Text in other languages cannot be compared or discussed together**: nowhere holds a translation. [T-049](tasks/T-049-translation-home.md), [T-112](tasks/T-112-translate-held-text.md) (the owner asked for it on 2026-11-12; the target language, English for display, is resolved under delegation as OD-02).

**Start now:** the tasks of Wave 0 need no owner decision, no design and no earlier wave (section 4). **Then stop for the owner** at the points listed in section 6; the questions are in section 8, each with a one-line answer form.

A task file never requires you to open these. |

The seven further suite documents first planned are not written; the owner dropped that plan in favour of this one.

## 2. How to execute

0. **Merge this workplan first.** The task files assume the workplan is on the branch a task starts from. Until its pull request is merged to `main`, the integration base is whichever remote branch carries the newest commit to this folder; every task file sets `$BASE` by one line that names no branch (`origin/main` when `main` contains that commit, otherwise the first remote branch that does), and gates and measures against it. A task started from a `main` that lacks the workplan would diff the whole workplan: the pilots showed it.
1. **One task, one session, one pull request.** Pick the next task by section 4 or 5. Open its file. Read `CLAUDE.md`. Do exactly what the file says, in its order: preconditions, evidence, change, sweep, verification, commit, adversarial pass, pull request last.
2. **One pull request merges at a time** (the prior workplan's rule WR-1: `grep -n "WR-1" workplan/2026-10-23-pipeline-resolution-workplan.md`). Branches may be prepared side by side; each later one takes the merged predecessor with `git merge origin/main` and derives its migration number again. Merging is the owner's act unless the owner has said otherwise; an executor does not merge its own pull request and does not watch it (CLAUDE.md rule 9).
3. **Tooling before research, never together** (CLAUDE.md rule 10). A research task starts only when the tooling it names is on `main`.
4. **A task that is `NOT FOR SONNET`** waits for the Fable implementation agent (design) or an Opus-class session (judgment), as its first line says. The owner authorised the Fable agent to "design, author, curate, orchestrate, delete as required" for code, schema, scripts, checks and skills (`grep -n -F "design, author, curate, orchestrate" references/project-standards.md`); doctrine stays with the owner.
5. **When a task stops**, it reports what it ran, what it saw and what it expected, and changes nothing further. A stop is a result, not a failure. Do not work around it.
5a. **The first execution of an unpiloted task is its pilot.** All but three of the task files have never been executed (section 12 says which, by command). The executor of each ends the pull request body with a heading "Task-file defects" listing what in the file was wrong, missing or ambiguous, even when the change succeeded, so the files that follow can be corrected.
6. **When the ground has moved** (a task's evidence command no longer gives the output the file states), the task stops. Either the defect is already fixed, or an earlier merge changed the facts; the orchestrating session re-reads the task against `main` before anyone resumes it.
7. **Nothing in this plan loosens a refusal the project holds on purpose.** The two refusals CLAUDE.md §4 says must stay absent stay absent.

## 8. Owner decision register

**Status after the delegated pass and the twelfth-instruction pass (2026-11-12).** Each entry below opens with its status. How many are resolved under delegation, referred back, still the owner's, or block a task is derived, never typed: run the gate loop of section 13 for the state of each, and a copy of `scratchpad/session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit/build_batches.py` whose `OUT` points outside the tree (the script writes `REMEDIATION-PLAN.md` despite its docstring: fact 12 of `DELEGATED-RESOLUTIONS-2-REVIEW.md`) for which of the CLOSED ones a task waits on (its last-but-one output line names the blocking and the standing sets; `REMEDIATION-PLAN.md` shows them with the tasks they release). The confirmation of each, with evidence, is `DECISION-CLOSURE.md`. A task no longer checks `grep -n -F "OD-NN:"`, which a delegated, a withdrawn and an owner's line all satisfied alike: it runs the ledger gate of section 13, which is OPEN only for an owner's answer, or for a delegated resolution whose independent check is not required or is recorded as confirmed. A task that needs the owner's words (T-102, T-053) opens only on an owner's answer. The rest of this register is as first written, so "Recommendation (the audit's …)" and "Tasks blocked until answered" describe the state before the pass; the status line says what holds now. **The second delegated pass (2026-11-13).** At the owner's question of 2026-11-13 (`grep -n -F "Owner question 2026-11-13 — may the open decisions OD-40 to OD-55" references/project-standards.md`), OD-40, OD-41, OD-42, OD-43, OD-45, OD-49, OD-50, OD-53 and OD-55 were resolved under the owner's twelfth instruction and confirmed with corrections by an independent check; OD-44, OD-46, OD-47, OD-48, OD-51, OD-52 and OD-54 were referred back and are put to the owner in plain words in `OWNER-SHEET-PLAIN.md`. Each of OD-40 to OD-55 keeps its registration status as an "Earlier status" line.

Each entry was written as **OWNER DECISION REQUIRED**; its status line says what holds now, and each recommendation is labelled as one. To answer, the owner says one of the answer forms; the session that hears it appends to `references/project-standards.md`, in the ledger's form, the owner's quoted words, the answer line `OD-NN: …`, and the status line with the value `ANSWERED BY THE OWNER` (a deferral takes `DEFERRED BY THE OWNER`; ledger convention and its addendum: `grep -n -F "Convention" references/project-standards.md | tail -2`). A task opens on the status line read through the gate of section 13, never on the `OD-NN:` line alone. OD-16 was withdrawn (it was answered on the record). Count the entries: `grep -c "^### OD-" workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md`.

**Which answers release the most work:** derived, not listed here: the "Blocking" table of `REMEDIATION-PLAN.md` gives, for each CLOSED decision a task waits on, the tasks it holds and every task waiting on those; `DECISION-CLOSURE.md` orders the owner's prompts by it. These ids belong to this plan; an older series with the same letters appears in `decisions/` and is unrelated.

### OD-01  Jurisdiction in a determination; jurisdictions below the country; climate and culture

- **Status (2026-11-12): RESOLVED UNDER DELEGATION** — not the owner's words; reversible by the owner; independent check (condition (d)) recorded as confirmed with corrections applied, `grep -n -F "Correction 2026-11-12 — to the delegated resolution of OD-01" references/project-standards.md`. Ledger: `grep -n -F "Delegated resolution 2026-11-12 — OD-01" references/project-standards.md`; reasoning: `DELEGATED-RESOLUTIONS.md`, section OD-01. **Blocks now:** nothing while its gate reads OPEN. **Read by:** T-024, T-036, T-113 (and T-037 through T-036).
- **Question.** Is there one determination per parameter and group, with the jurisdictions shown beside it as a spread, or one determination per jurisdiction? Is a province, state or region a jurisdiction of its own? Are climate and cultural context recorded as typed conditions?
- **Why it is the owner's.** Jurisdiction scope and the shape of the book's central claim are doctrine. The ledger holds no ruling on the cell key carrying a jurisdiction.
- **Options and what follows from each.**

# T-028 design — a concept is its id; its names are forms; `canonical_en` is our label

_Written 2026-11-12 by an Opus-class designer under the owner's instruction "Opus to write design files that must be written first", on the delegated resolution of OD-03. Plan document: it changes no script, schema, row or ruling. Every count is given as the command that produces it; re-run it. SQL marked **sketch** is a shape, not a file to paste unread. Canadian English._

_Revised 2026-11-13, after the T-028 pilot (`scratchpad/session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit/pilot/T-028-report.md`) and the fold of T-026: no pointer reaches `term_aliases` by `rowid` (SQLite cannot declare a foreign key on one and `emit_batch_sql.py` does not carry implicit rowids), so T-026's junction is keyed and T-028 remaps it by key to `form_id`; `attestation` keeps T-026's `DEFAULT`; the judge, reason and former label of every label set by judgment get one typed home, `term_label_picks`, which also holds the base route's rationale; the refusals of `rename-term` and `mint-term-from-catalogue` are kept, and one cross-language question is left to the owner; `label_is_instrument_term` is renamed `label_is_attested_form`. Where the 2026-11-12 text and this revision differ, the revision governs._

## 0. Verdict

**The one table that holds a form is `term_aliases`.** No new forms table is built. T-026 puts the attestation and locator columns on it (names fixed in section 4 so the two tasks agree). T-028 then rebuilds it to one row per **occurrence**, keyed by a new `form_id` (equal to each existing row's `rowid`), with a unique occurrence index in place of today's primary key `(term_id, alias, language)`, and adds `usage_type`. In the same migration it remaps T-026's search-to-form junction from the old key to `form_id`, by key, and adds `term_label_picks`, the one home of the judge, the reason and the former label of a label set by judgment (OD-38). A concept's identity stays `terms.term_id`; its equivalence class is its member rows in `term_aliases`. **`terms.canonical_en` stays `TEXT NOT NULL`, as our English descriptive label: never written as a form, never read first.** (A new label is screened against other concepts' labels and attested forms so that one phrase does not point at two concepts, section 8.) Whether the label is also an instrument's term, and the name shown (E1), are derived by one view, `v_term_names`; the only stored choice is the label itself, changed by `rename-term` with its warrant. Five writers change: the two name screens (`_name_holder`, `_near_terms`) become attestation-aware and stop making English the pivot for a non-English name; `add-term` gains a base route that mints a concept with its first attested form and stops forcing a non-English concept's label to sit inside the source's phrase (the defect AT-25 exposes); `rename-term` stops writing our former label as a form or as a `scope_note` trailer and gains `--from-form`, every route naming its judge; `add-alias` refuses the legacy relation values and records an occurrence, not a key.

**Confidence.** Medium-high (about 75%) that `term_aliases` is the right single home: the alternative (`term_forms`, the 2026-11-06 matrix design) leaves 2382 baseline rows in a second table that can never be emptied (section 2). Medium (about 60%) on the display rule's tie-break (section 7, rule 2), which is deterministic but arbitrary when several English instruments use different forms.

**Owner's call.** None is outstanding: OD-03 is resolved under delegation (`grep -F "OD-03 STATUS:" references/project-standards.md | tail -1`; its check is `not required`), reversible by the owner. The points at which the owner may disagree are listed in section 15; the one most likely to matter is the tie-break of section 7.

## 1. What the rulings require

| Ruling (find it with) | Requirement | Met by |
|---|---|---|
| OD-03 (delegated), `grep -n -F 'OD-03: forms table' references/project-standards.md` | identity is the neutral id; names are rows of one forms table, one row per occurrence with language, jurisdiction, source; `canonical_en` our label, never a form; label basis derived; display by E1; a stored choice only where no derivation decides | sections 3, 6, 7 |
| Sixth statement 2026-11-06, `grep -n -F 'a concept is an equivalence class of forms' references/project-standards.md` | equivalence class; usage type and attestation per form; disfavoured forms kept; conflation recorded per occurrence, not resolved | member rows; `usage_type`; T-026's `attestation`; conflation derived (section 5) |
| Seventh statement 2026-11-06, `grep -n -F 'base grounds itself' references/project-standards.md` | a base form carries its own source columns (URL, page, line), not an `evidence_sources` row | T-026's locator columns; `add-term` base route (section 8) |
| Eighth statement 2026-11-06, `grep -n -F 'English labels are allowed on non-English-origin concepts' references/project-standards.md` | an English label allowed, marked as ours; the instrument's phrase kept as a form; no English form until an English-jurisdiction source uses one; no column read, matched or ranked first | `canonical_en` as label; `v_term_names.label_is_attested_form`; screens per language (section 8) |
| E1 and E4, `grep -n -E '^\| E1 |^\| E4 ' references/project-standards.md` | E1: named by the instrument's own phrase until an English-language instrument of a P1+P2+P3 jurisdiction names it. E4: model-generated and unrecorded aliases stay as flagged search aids, never vocabulary, never deleted | `v_term_names` rules (section 7); screens read attested forms only (section 8) |
| CLAUDE.md rule 5 and the 2026-11-06 schema-shape statement | one home per fact; one value per cell | one forms table; `usage_type` and `attestation` in their own cells; legacy `alias_type` values frozen (section 5) |

## 2. Why `term_aliases`, not a new `term_forms`

- **One home.** `term_aliases` already holds every name the base has (`select count(*) from term_aliases`). Its rows were inserted by the 057 baseline (`grep -c 'INSERT INTO "term_aliases"' scripts/migrations/057_baseline_2026-08-12.sql`), and the 2026-09-16 ruling retires data rows in place, never deleting them. A new `term_forms` beside it leaves those rows where they are forever: either copied (two homes) or reached through a union view (the matrix design's `v_base_lookup`), which is two homes joined at read time.
- **The matrix design's two objections are answered in place.** (i) "The PK has no jurisdiction or source": the rebuild replaces the PK by a surrogate key and an occurrence index that includes jurisdiction and locator (section 3). (ii) "It mixes model seeds with attested forms": T-026's typed `attestation` separates them in a cell, and every vocabulary read filters on it (section 8).
- **The name stays.** Renaming the table would make every caller a sweep item (`git grep -l -F term_aliases -- scripts schemas .github .claude skills ':(exclude)scripts/migrations'` and the prose `git grep` of the task file) for a legibility gain only; a row of `term_aliases` is documented as "a form of the concept, or a related search string" (section 5).
## 5. Membership, the legacy `alias_type` values, and conflation

- **Members of the equivalence class** are the rows whose `alias_type` is not `NARROWER` or `BROADER`. A `NARROWER` or `BROADER` row is a related search string, not a name of the concept: it is never shown as a name, never counted as a form, never matched as a name. (Term-to-term relations are T-029's table; these strings name no term.)
- **`TRANSLATION`, `DEPRECATED`, `DOMAIN` are legacy values.** Each joins a relation with another fact (a seed's origin; a usage; a domain variant). After T-026 and T-028 those facts have typed homes (`attestation`, `usage_type`). The existing rows are **not rewritten** (`DOMAIN` cannot be mapped to a usage without judgment: `select alias, language, notes from term_aliases where alias_type='DOMAIN'`); no writer writes these three values again; no reader infers attestation or usage from them. `add-alias` already refuses `TRANSLATION` and `DEPRECATED`; it now refuses `DOMAIN` too, naming `--usage-type`. `rename-term` stops writing `DEPRECATED` (section 8).
- **Conflation is derived, not stored:** a form held as a member by two concepts in one language is a conflation. Query: `select upper(language), alias, group_concat(distinct term_id) from term_aliases where alias_type not in ('NARROWER','BROADER') group by 1, 2 having count(distinct term_id) > 1`. `add-alias` reports it; `add-term` refuses it unless the operator names the other concept with `--distinct-from`; `rename-term` and `mint-term-from-catalogue` refuse a label another concept holds as an attested form, as they do today (section 8; corrected 2026-11-13).

## 6. `canonical_en`

- **Kept, `NOT NULL`, meaning "our English descriptive label".** Six committed data migrations INSERT `terms.canonical_en` (`git grep -l canonical_en -- 'scripts/migrations/data_*' | wc -l`) and six views read it as a parameter's name (`select name from sqlite_master where type='view' and sql like '%canonical_en%'`); every one keeps working because the column keeps its meaning: a label to show and to search our own registry by. Relaxing `NOT NULL` would rebuild `terms` for no gain once English labels are allowed (eighth statement).
- **Never a form.** No writer copies `canonical_en` into `term_aliases`. `rename-term` stops doing so (it wrote the old label as `DEPRECATED`); the former label is recorded once, in `term_label_picks.former_label` (section 3). **Corrected 2026-11-13:** this page first kept it in the `AMENDED` trailer `rename-term` writes on `scope_note`, which the 2026-11-06 schema-shape statement forbids (a correction appended to a note); no route of `rename-term` writes that trailer now, and existing trailers are not rewritten.
- **Marked as ours by derivation, not a column** (OD-03: "add no label-kind column"): `v_term_names.label_is_attested_form` is 1 exactly when an attested member form (`instrument` or `other_source`) of the same concept has the label's text. (Named `label_is_instrument_term` until 2026-11-13; it was never restricted to instruments.) Otherwise the label is ours.
- **The 94 terms** (`select count(*) from terms`) are unchanged; every one derives `label_is_attested_form = 0` today, because no row is attested yet (`select count(*) from term_aliases where observation_id is not null` prints 0, and T-026's fill adds no locator).
- The rule that a label must sit inside an observed phrase (the owner's 2026-09-09 rule, kept 2026-10-09) **still binds when the first form is English**; it is lifted only for a concept whose first form is not English, where the eighth statement allows an English descriptive label.

## 7. The name shown: `v_term_names` (E1 derived; sketch)
## 9. Pointers to other homes

- **Translations (T-049).** A translation of a form is a `translations` row pointing at `('term_aliases', 'alias', <form_id>)`, never an alias and never a term; a concept is minted only from an observed or located phrase (no back-translation). The English label is **not** a translation of any form and is never stored as one. **Corrected 2026-11-13:** this page said a pointer made by `rowid` before T-028 "survives, since `form_id` is the old `rowid`". It survives a rebuild, but not the capture: `emit_batch_sql.py` does not carry implicit rowids (section 4), so a rowid written on a scratch copy can name another row in the canonical database, and before T-028 `term_aliases` has a composite key that a single `source_row_key` cell does not hold without an encoding nobody has defined. So no translation points into `term_aliases` before T-028: T-049's file, as folded on 2026-11-13, already says so (`request-translation` refuses a table whose declared primary key has more than one column, and never points by `rowid`). After T-028 a translation points at `form_id`, which the migration preserves, so nothing is remapped; if `translations` nevertheless holds a row pointing into `term_aliases` at execution, T-028 stops rather than guess its encoding (the task file's section 9).
- **`value_as_written` (T-008)** is the same principle at the grain of a figure: the source's words in a cell that names them (`term_aliases.alias`, with its locator), our reading in a cell that names it ours (`canonical_en`). No second mechanism is built.
- **`observed_terms`** stays the evidence-stage record of a sighting; a member row points at it by `observation_id` where it came that way.

## 10. Migration shape (one schema migration; derive its number, never type it)

## 15. Rejected alternatives, and where the owner may disagree

- **A. A new `term_forms` table (the 2026-11-06 matrix design).** Leaves the 2382 rows in a second home (section 2).
- **B. Relax `canonical_en` to nullable and name a non-English concept by its phrase in that column.** Rebuilds `terms` under six views; puts a form in the label's cell, the opposite of OD-03.
- **C. A typed label-kind column on `terms`.** OD-03 forbids it: derivable, and a typed value can only be right or wrong.
- **D. A stored display pointer on `terms`.** A second home for the choice `rename-term` already stores in the label with its warrant; it could disagree with the forms.
- **E. Rewrite the legacy `alias_type` values in the migration.** `DOMAIN` needs judgment per row; a mechanical rewrite would invent usages.
- **F. Put the occurrence grain into T-026.** Turns a column addition into a rebuild for a Sonnet task, while T-028 rebuilds the table anyway; instead T-107 waits for T-028.
- **G. The judge and reason as columns on `terms`** (2026-11-13). A later rename would overwrite them, so they would describe a pick no longer in force, and the former label would still need a home; one row per pick in `term_label_picks` keeps each. It is not alternative D: `v_term_names` does not read it.
- **H. The base route's rationale in the first form's `notes`** (the pilot's choice). A judgment about the concept in a cell about one form, which the 2026-11-06 schema-shape statement forbids; and T-026 rules out a rationale in `notes` for `add-alias`'s base route too.

**Where the owner may disagree:** (1) [ANSWERED 2026-11-12, OD-38: first recorded until a named judge picks, the pick recorded with its reason] the tie-break of section 7, rule 2 (first recorded English instrument form) against showing our label when several English instruments differ; (2) lifting the inside-the-phrase rule only for non-English first forms (section 6); (3) the label clash being checked only for English names (a non-English candidate's English label is still screened, as a label); (4) **open, the owner's (2026-11-13):** whether an identical string attested in one language for one concept clashes with a name in another language for a different concept, or is an independent form. It is a question of what the sixth statement's conflation and the eighth statement's "English is one column" mean across languages, not of code. Until it is answered the exact screen keeps today's reach (attested forms in every language; section 8), and the task file's section 9 stops on any step that would narrow it.

**Not resolved here, reported:** the base coverage view the seventh statement makes the acceptance test is T-057's (AT-23; corrected 2026-11-13: this page said no task builds it); `v_term_names`, the occurrence grain and the junction by `form_id` are what it reads.

def _near_terms(conn, name: str) -> list:
    """Terms whose canonical name or ATTESTED alias, in any language (T-009), shares a token set with `name` one
    way or the other (subset or superset): 'ramp runs' beside 'ramp run length',
    'reverberations' beside 'reverberation time'. The equivalence search the skill tells an
    operator to do before minting, done by the writer and refused unless each is named
    --distinct-from. Exact matches are _name_holder's; this is the near miss nothing checked
    (2026-11-06).

    An alias compares unless its `attestation` is model_seed (T-026): a known unattested
    seed is a search aid, so it neither names a concept nor blocks a new one. An `unrecorded`
    or owner_supplied alias is STILL compared, as before 130: E4 (whether a form without a
    locator is vocabulary) is an open owner question, and a live refusal is not weakened on
    the strength of an open question. The label comparison is unchanged."""
    want = _name_tokens(name)
    if not want:
        return []
    out, seen = [], set()
    for term_id, held in conn.execute(
            "SELECT term_id, canonical_en FROM terms UNION ALL "
            "SELECT term_id, alias FROM term_aliases WHERE attestation <> 'model_seed'"):
        have = _name_tokens(held)
        # Near: the new name's tokens sit inside an existing name's ('ramp runs' in 'ramp run
        # length'), or an existing name of TWO OR MORE tokens sits inside the new one. A
        # one-token term ('ramp') inside every compound that mentions it is not a near match,
        # or no compound could ever be minted (measured on the replay, 2026-11-06).
        near = have and have != want and (want <= have or (have <= want and len(have) >= 2))
        if near and term_id not in seen:
            seen.add(term_id)
            out.append((term_id, held))
    return out

def retire_parameter(parameter_id: int, reason: str, session: str, dry_run: bool = False):
    """Retire a parameter IN PLACE: status 'retired', the reason appended to its notes.

    Owner ruling 2026-09-16, "retire in place then": no row is deleted and the number is
    never reissued (base_parameters is AUTOINCREMENT, migration 076). The parameter's
    extractions, readings and history stay; every reader that lists or counts parameters
    filters on status (v_scan_ledger, v_value_independence since 104), and the writers
    already refuse an inactive parameter (add-extraction, raise-determination-gate,
    assess_cell's validate_parameter).

    REFUSES: a blank reason; a parameter that is not active (retired already, or merged
    -- its survivor is where work goes); a LIVE determination or an OPEN gate on it.
    """
    reason = dbcore.require_reason(
        reason, f"parameter {parameter_id}",
        why="A retirement that cannot say why cannot be reviewed or reversed by decision.")
    with connect(dry_run) as conn:
        row = _parameter_row(conn, parameter_id, "retire-parameter")
        if row["status"] != "active":
            target = f" into {row['merged_into']}" if row["merged_into"] else ""
            raise Refusal(
                f"retire-parameter: parameter {parameter_id} ({row['canonical_en']!r}) is "
                f"already {row['status']}{target}. Nothing was written.")
        _refuse_live_work(conn, parameter_id, "retire-parameter")
        stamp = dbcore.now()
        notes = dbcore.append_dated_note(row["notes"], "RETIRED", session, reason, stamp)
        sets = {"status": "retired", "notes": notes}
        sets.update(_updated(conn, "base_parameters", session, stamp))
        conn.execute("UPDATE base_parameters SET " + ", ".join(f"{k} = ?" for k in sets)
                     + " WHERE parameter_id = ?", list(sets.values()) + [parameter_id])
        kept = conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM source_value_extractions "
                            "WHERE parameter_id = ?", (parameter_id,)).fetchone()[0]
        return {"parameter_id": parameter_id, "canonical_en": row["canonical_en"],
                "status": "retired", "extractions_kept_as_history": kept,
                "dry_run": dry_run}


def merge_parameter(from_id: int, into_id: int, reason: str, session: str,
                    dry_run: bool = False):
    """Fold parameter `from_id` into `into_id`: two names for one quantity become one.

    Sets the folded row to status 'merged' with merged_into = the survivor -- the shape
    base_parameters' own CHECK has carried since 071 with no writer -- and RE-POINTS
    every row that holds the folded parameter_id at the survivor, with a dated MERGED
    line appended to each moved row's notes, in one transaction. The set of tables is
    READ FROM THE LIVE SCHEMA (every foreign key into base_parameters.parameter_id,
    including base_parameters.merged_into, so a chain of merges flattens onto the
    survivor); `_MERGE_KEEPS_HISTORY` is the only exception list, each entry with its
    reason. A table that holds the id but has no notes column is refused rather than
    moved silently.

    REFUSES: the same id twice; a blank reason; either parameter not active; a LIVE
    determination or an OPEN gate on either. K02 then holds the survivor's next
    determination to every extraction it gained.
    """
    if from_id == into_id:
        raise Refusal("merge-parameter: --from and --into are the same parameter.")
    reason = dbcore.require_reason(
        reason, f"merge {from_id} -> {into_id}",
        why="A merge that cannot say why two names are one quantity cannot be reviewed.")
    with connect(dry_run) as conn:
        a = _parameter_row(conn, from_id, "merge-parameter --from")
        b = _parameter_row(conn, into_id, "merge-parameter --into")
        for r, side in ((a, "--from"), (b, "--into")):
            if r["status"] != "active":
                raise Refusal(
                    f"merge-parameter {side}: parameter {r['parameter_id']} "
                    f"({r['canonical_en']!r}) is {r['status']}, not active. Nothing was "
                    f"written.")
        _refuse_live_work(conn, from_id, "merge-parameter --from")
        _refuse_live_work(conn, into_id, "merge-parameter --into")
        stamp = dbcore.now()
        line = f"parameter_id {from_id} -> {into_id} (merge-parameter): {reason}"
        moved, kept = {}, {}
        tables = [t for (t,) in conn.execute(
            "SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table' ORDER BY name")]
        for t in tables:
            for fk in conn.execute(f'PRAGMA foreign_key_list("{t}")').fetchall():
                if fk[2] != "base_parameters" or (fk[4] or "parameter_id") != "parameter_id":
                    continue
                col = fk[3]
                n = conn.execute(f'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "{t}" WHERE "{col}" = ?',
                                 (from_id,)).fetchone()[0]
                if not n:
                    continue
                if t in _MERGE_KEEPS_HISTORY:
                    kept[f"{t}.{col}"] = n
                    continue
                cols = dbcore.columns(conn, t)
                if "notes" not in cols:
                    raise Refusal(
                        f"merge-parameter: {t}.{col} holds {n} row(s) for parameter "
                        f"{from_id} and the table has no notes column to record the move "
                        f"on. Moving them silently would leave no trace on the rows; add "
                        f"the table to _MERGE_KEEPS_HISTORY with its reason, or give it a "
                        f"notes column, in a tooling PR. Nothing was written.")
                info = conn.execute(f'PRAGMA table_info("{t}")').fetchall()
                pk = [r[1] for r in sorted((r for r in info if r[5]), key=lambda r: r[5])]
                key = pk or ["rowid"]
                rows = conn.execute(
                    f'SELECT {", ".join(chr(34) + k + chr(34) for k in key)}, notes '
                    f'FROM "{t}" WHERE "{col}" = ?', (from_id,)).fetchall()
                for r in rows:
                    sets = {col: into_id,
                            "notes": dbcore.append_dated_note(r["notes"], "MERGED",
                                                              session, line, stamp)}
                    sets.update(_updated(conn, t, session, stamp))
                    try:
                        conn.execute(
                            f'UPDATE "{t}" SET ' + ", ".join(f'"{k}" = ?' for k in sets)
                            + " WHERE " + " AND ".join(f'"{k}" = ?' for k in key),
                            list(sets.values()) + [r[k] for k in key])
                    except sqlite3.IntegrityError as exc:
                        raise Refusal(
                            f"merge-parameter: re-pointing {t}.{col} collided with a row "
                            f"the survivor already holds ({exc}). Resolve that row first. "
                            f"Nothing was written.") from exc
                moved[f"{t}.{col}"] = len(rows)
        notes = dbcore.append_dated_note(
            a["notes"], "MERGED", session,
            f"merged into parameter {into_id} ({b['canonical_en']!r}): {reason}", stamp)
        sets = {"status": "merged", "merged_into": into_id, "notes": notes}
        sets.update(_updated(conn, "base_parameters", session, stamp))
        conn.execute("UPDATE base_parameters SET " + ", ".join(f"{k} = ?" for k in sets)
                     + " WHERE parameter_id = ?", list(sets.values()) + [from_id])
        return {"from": from_id, "into": into_id, "from_name": a["canonical_en"],
                "into_name": b["canonical_en"], "re_pointed": moved,
                "kept_as_history": kept, "dry_run": dry_run}


def annotate_parameter(parameter_id: int, note: str, session: str, dry_run: bool = False):
    """Append a dated, attributed line to a parameter's notes. Never overwrites.

    The correction route a wrong note lacked (critique F18: parameter 12's note says "no
    source adjudication behind it" while TERM-091 carries a NAMES-NEW adjudication). Any
    status: correcting the record of a retired parameter is still a correction.
    """
    note = (note or "").strip()
    if not note:
        raise Refusal("annotate-parameter: --note is required and may not be blank.")
    if " || " in note:
        raise Refusal("annotate-parameter: --note contains ' || ', the separator every "
                      "dated line in notes begins with; it would make one annotation read "
                      "as two. Nothing was written.")
    with connect(dry_run) as conn:
        row = _parameter_row(conn, parameter_id, "annotate-parameter")
        stamp = dbcore.now()
        sets = {"notes": dbcore.append_dated_note(row["notes"], "ANNOTATED", session,
                                                  note, stamp)}
        sets.update(_updated(conn, "base_parameters", session, stamp))
        conn.execute("UPDATE base_parameters SET " + ", ".join(f"{k} = ?" for k in sets)
                     + " WHERE parameter_id = ?", list(sets.values()) + [parameter_id])
        return {"parameter_id": parameter_id, "annotated": True, "dry_run": dry_run}


def _alias_language(conn, language: str) -> str:
    """`language` in the letter case `term_aliases` itself uses, measured, not assumed.

    observed_terms stores 'EN' and term_aliases stores 'en' (catalogue-plan-v2 section
    1.2 item 4). A phrase observed in 'DE' and an alias in 'de' are the same language,
    and a primary key that compared them as different would admit the same alias twice.
    """
    lo, up = conn.execute(
        "SELECT SUM(language = lower(language)), SUM(language = upper(language)) "
        "FROM term_aliases").fetchone()
    return language.lower() if (lo or 0) >= (up or 0) else language.upper()


def _names_term(conn, observation_id: int, term_id: str) -> bool:
    """Does the LATEST adjudication of this observation name this term?

    Adjudications are appended, never edited (adjudicate_term: a disagreeing judgment is a second
    row), so the latest one is the observation's standing judgment; an earlier one that named the
    term and was later declined or re-pointed warrants nothing. Latest = highest adjudication_id
    (the order the writer assigns; created_at is minute-resolution and can tie)."""
    row = conn.execute(
        "SELECT term_id FROM term_adjudications WHERE observation_id = ? "
        "ORDER BY adjudication_id DESC LIMIT 1", (observation_id,)).fetchone()
    return row is not None and row[0] == term_id


def _not_named_msg(conn, verb: str, observation_id: int, term_id: str) -> str:
    """The refusal's opening, shared by the callers of _names_term: it says WHICH case holds."""
    row = conn.execute(
        "SELECT adjudication_id, outcome, term_id, created_by_session FROM term_adjudications "
        "WHERE observation_id = ? ORDER BY adjudication_id DESC LIMIT 1", (observation_id,)).fetchone()
    if row is None:
        what = "there is none"
    elif row["term_id"]:
        what = f"adjudication {row['adjudication_id']} ({row['created_by_session']}) names {row['term_id']}"
    else:
        what = f"adjudication {row['adjudication_id']} ({row['created_by_session']}) is {row['outcome']}"
    return (f"{verb}: the latest adjudication of observation {observation_id} does not name {term_id}: {what}.")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""scripts/audit/derivation_handshake_integrity.py — the handshake, checked on the rows.

WHAT WRONG THING REACHES THE *GUIDEBOOK* IF THIS DOES NOT EXIST (CLAUDE.md §8's bar,
which is about the book and not the apparatus):

  1. A `stated` determination sitting under an OPEN, BINDING gate. The book asserts a
     best-practice value while an audit has already said its population links are wrong,
     or that a source of equal-or-greater strength contradicts it. H4's whole content is
     that such a cell reads `provisional` "until resolved"; a cap that fails silently is
     indistinguishable from a cap that was never applied.
  2. A CULTURAL CLAIM ANCHOR THAT ANCHORS NOTHING — and this is the one the schema

Order of preference, from CLAUDE.md §8: do nothing and say why; change a rule or convention; reuse what exists; delete the cause; only then add the smallest code that closes the defect.

1. **The clause inventory (the owner's route).** One table of clause rows: each row is one clause of one source, keyed by the source (`ref_id`), the locator columns `source_value_extractions` already uses (`locator_scheme`, `loc_*`), the `scan_id` of the reading that recorded it, and the clause's text as held for matching. One home: a figure's extraction points at its clause row, never repeats its locator in a second place it does not already hold. The open pass of a full reading (`source_scans.open_pass_done`) writes the inventory.
2. **Held clause text is not shown** (the owner: "clause NOT shown"). No view a page reads selects the clause text; the render task (T-037) reads clause rows only for their locators. A test asserts that no `v_*` view the renderer reads names the text column (derive the renderer's views from T-037 when it lands; until then, from the views whose names the render contract lists).
3. **Backed by retained text.** A later parameter is matched first against the inventory, then by a sweep over the retained text (the committed artefact named by the scan's `file_sha256`), and only where neither reaches is the source read again.
4. **The re-read flag, derived and not stored** (the owner: "We can flag a source to be read again for later parameters"; smallest change, one home). A pair (source × parameter) is *owed* already, derived by `v_scan_ledger` and printed by `scripts/audit/scan_debt.py` (`DEBT:`). The flag is that derivation narrowed: owed, **and** no inventory row of the source matches the parameter, **and** no retained text is on disk for the source's latest full scan. It is a view (or a `--reread` mode of `scan_debt.py`), never a column or a table of its own, so it cannot drift from the scans; it is cleared by recording the reading (`record-scan --mode targeted`, or `catalogue`). ## Delegated resolution 2026-11-12 — OD-11 which stage owns the gap register

A resolution by an Opus-class model under the owner's delegation of 2026-11-12, judged against the owner's three criteria; **not the owner's words**; standing until the owner reverses it. Reasoning and evidence: `workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/DELEGATED-RESOLUTIONS.md` (section OD-11).

OD-11: cross-stage register

**The resolution.** The gap register is written by whichever stage finds the gap; each gap names the stage that raised it (from the pipeline contract's stage ids) and what it is a gap in. The stage map marks it cross-stage, and the walkability instrument must count it as a member of each stage it carries, verified by running the instrument before and after the change.

**What decided it.** Gaps are already written by research sessions and the engine and pointed at from judgment and specification; confining them to research would forbid the gap the absent-cell resolution requires (criteria 1 and 3). The stage map's own dispute note reached the same answer.

**Reversal condition.** The stage map gaining a stage for it, or the owner assigning gaps to one stage.

CONDITION: any session writing a gap, mapping tables to stages, or changing the walkability instrument.
ACTION: (1) Let any stage raise a gap, naming itself. (2) Mark the register cross-stage in the stage map. (3) Run the walkability instrument before and after; lose no path.
DATE: 2026-11-12 — delegated resolution, not an owner statement.


## Delegated resolution 2026-11-12 — OD-12 how render's prose is produced, and whether it is stored

A resolution by an Opus-class model under the owner's delegation of 2026-11-12, judged against the owner's three criteria; **not the owner's words**; standing until the owner reverses it; **not to be relied on until the independent check of condition (d) is recorded**. It answers the owner-queue prompts OW-1b and OW-1c. Reasoning and evidence: `workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/DELEGATED-RESOLUTIONS.md` (section OD-12).

OD-12: templates, rebuilt

**The resolution.** Render assembles every sentence by templates held in one place from typed rows, and writes no prose of its own judgment. Discussion that needs judgment (a divergence approach, a relation, a caveat) is a synthesis-stage row written at the Opus floor with its warrant and quoted by pointer. def sha(parameter_id, lens, links, conditioned=()):
    """Cell-scoped derivation sha: parameter + the three lens codes + the graded link set + the
    conditioned governing claims + rule version, so pending cells do not all share one constant
    hash and staleness stays checkable.

    The payload is byte-for-byte what test_db_integrity K01 recomputes when it verifies a stored
    sha. Two implementations of one hash that disagree is a hash that attests nothing, so this one
    and K01's move together or not at all. `lens` is the code dict from pilot-6 on (four slots to pilot-6, three from pilot-7), joined with
    `|` in LENS_ORDER (a code never contains the separator, so two splits of the same characters
    across two models cannot collide); the earlier link-set labels hashed the COALESCE key
    (`lens_key()`), which K01 keeps for them (COALESCE_LENS_SHA_VERSIONS). The links are
    `link_payload()`: each extraction's role and whether the cell's lens reaches it (pilot-6).
    `conditioned` (pilot-5) is `conditioned_governing()`, hashed as a `|branches:` term only when
    non-empty; K01 recomputes it from `extraction_relations`.

    THE SHA IS NOT A COUNT OF EVIDENCE. Before migration 077 it hashed an unfiltered extraction
    count so that a parameter never read and one read and rejected hashed differently; the graded
    links say the same thing, and each extraction of the parameter the cell reaches is among them,
    so the sha moves when evidence for the parameter is added or a figure leaves the cell's lens,
    not only when the stored row is edited. That is the doctrine it was built for: evidence-
    architecture §10 mechanical check 2, "same evidence + same rule_version => same state + same
    derivation_sha". A determination stamped before an extraction arrived, or before a lens link
    was added or retired, IS stale, and K01 saying so is the check working.

    # The branch term (pilot-5): the governing claims that hold only under a condition

RESOLUTION IS A SEPARATE VERB, deliberately. `resolve-determination-gate` exists
    because resolution "is a NAMED PATH -- evidence-auditor adjudication recorded on the
    cell together with its rationale -- so no cell sits at `provisional` with no owner of
    resolution". Letting this verb create an already-resolved row would permit a gate
    that never bound anything, which the table's own CHECK cannot catch because the shape
    is legal -- the same reason `add-parameter` takes no --status.
    """
    detail = (detail or "").strip()
    if not detail:
        raise Refusal(
            "--detail is required and may not be blank. A gate that cannot say what it "
            "found is a cell pinned at provisional for no stated reason, which is the "
            "deadlock the resolution discipline exists to prevent.")
    if verdict == "QUESTION":
        # A question states no strength: no source raised it, so no tier is invented for it (OD-21). The
        # engine reports it beside the cell and never lets it cap the cell.
        if trigger_ref_id or trigger_tier is not None or trigger_evidence_type:
            raise Refusal(
                "a QUESTION carries no --trigger-ref-id, --trigger-tier or --trigger-evidence-type: it is an "
                "objection to a published value, not a finding with a strength, and a tier typed onto it "
                "would let it pin a cell, or fail to, on a strength nobody established. Put the objection "
                "in --detail. To raise a finding that a source supports, use a verdict other than QUESTION.")
    elif trigger_ref_id and (trigger_tier is not None or trigger_evidence_type):
        raise Refusal(
            "--trigger-tier / --trigger-evidence-type are refused alongside "
            "--trigger-ref-id. The source states both, and this row POINTS at the "
            "source (rule 5); they are read from it. A typed tier is a tier that can be "
            "typed wrong, and a wrong one inverts the ladder the gate exists to protect.")
    if verdict != "QUESTION" and not trigger_ref_id and (trigger_tier is None or not trigger_evidence_type):
        raise Refusal(
            "a gate with no --trigger-ref-id must state --trigger-tier and "
            "--trigger-evidence-type. Doctrine requires every gate to carry the strength "
            "of what raised it, so a grey-tier finding cannot pin a T1-anchored cell. A "
            "gate that cannot say how strong its trigger was inverts the ladder by "
            "omission.")

CREATE TABLE "determination_gates" (
    gate_id             INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    parameter_id        INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES base_parameters(parameter_id),
    -- The lens the finding applies to, NULL meaning every lens on this parameter. Not an FK set like
    -- specifications' four, because a gate is raised against a parameter by an audit that may not know which cells
    -- exist yet. A gate is skipped for a cell only when the cell carries a DIFFERENT code in a lens the gate names; a lens the cell does not carry never skips it (the rule the identity column always had).
    identity_code       TEXT REFERENCES "base_taxonomy_identity"(identity_code),
    icf_code            TEXT REFERENCES base_icf(icf_code),
    needs_code          TEXT REFERENCES access_needs(need_code),
    verdict             TEXT NOT NULL
                        CHECK (verdict IN ('UNLINKED', 'MISLINKED',
                                           'UNDER-CONSERVATIVE', 'CONTRADICTS', 'QUESTION')),
    -- The ladder-inversion guard: how strong the thing raising the gate actually is. A QUESTION has no such
    -- thing and carries NULL in all three trigger columns; every other verdict states them.
    trigger_ref_id      TEXT REFERENCES evidence_sources(ref_id),
    trigger_tier        INTEGER CHECK (trigger_tier BETWEEN 1 AND 6),
    trigger_evidence_type TEXT,
    detail              TEXT NOT NULL,
    raised_at           TEXT NOT NULL,
    raised_by_session   TEXT NOT NULL,
    resolved_at         TEXT,
    resolved_by_session TEXT,
    resolution_rationale TEXT,
    CHECK ((resolved_at IS NULL AND resolved_by_session IS NULL
            AND resolution_rationale IS NULL)
        OR (resolved_at IS NOT NULL AND resolved_by_session IS NOT NULL
            AND resolution_rationale IS NOT NULL)),
    CHECK ((verdict = 'QUESTION'
            AND trigger_tier IS NULL AND trigger_evidence_type IS NULL AND trigger_ref_id IS NULL)
        OR (verdict <> 'QUESTION'
            AND trigger_tier IS NOT NULL AND trigger_evidence_type IS NOT NULL))
)
CREATE VIEW v_open_determination_gates AS
SELECT g.gate_id, g.parameter_id, g.identity_code, g.icf_code, g.needs_code, g.verdict,
       g.trigger_ref_id, g.trigger_tier, g.trigger_evidence_type, g.detail,
       g.raised_at, g.raised_by_session
  FROM determination_gates g
 WHERE g.resolved_at IS NULL
