# T-129 design — a merge of two terms is a row, the survivor is derived, and the consolidation sweep proposes, a judge decides, and it ends

_Written 2026-11-17 by an Opus-class adjudicator on the owner's instruction of 2026-11-16 ("have Opus collate all of my questions about this and all of your answers/findings then adjudicate best fixes before planning out how to build followed by folding it into remediation plan"; "ensure compliance with layer architecture, prioritize long-term integrity of project re provenance and consistency"). Plan document: it changes no script, schema, row or ruling. Every count is given as the command that produces it; re-run it. SQL marked **sketch** is a shape, not a file to paste unread. Canadian English. It governs two tasks: section A is T-129 (the merge, NOT FOR SONNET), section B is T-130 (the proposer and its bound, a Sonnet-class executor may run it from this file). The adjudication that chose it is `workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/PROPAGATION-AND-CONSOLIDATION-ADJUDICATION.md`._

## 0. Verdict

**Two terms judged to name one concept are merged by a row, never by rewriting the rows that point at them.** A new base table, `term_merges`, holds one row per merge (the folded term, its survivor, who judged it, when, why) and retires in place when a merge is undone. One view, `v_term_survivor`, follows the live merges to each term's survivor; it is the single home of "which concept is this term now". Rows of every stage that point at the folded term keep pointing at it (they record what their writer said, when it said it); every writer that takes a term id resolves it through the view and refuses a folded term, naming the survivor; every name screen and every reader of a concept's forms reads the survivor's class (its own forms and those of every term folded into it). A judgment that two near-named terms are **not** one concept is a typed row of T-029's term-relation table, kind `distinct`, with its warrant; `add-term --distinct-from` writes it instead of leaving the judgment in the adjudication's free-text rationale.

**The sweep is a read verb, a bound held in the contract, and the batch.** `db.py consolidation-candidates` proposes pairs of live concepts that may be one (four derived reasons, each with the rows that show it); an Opus-class session judges each (merge, relate, distinct, or leave); a judged pair is not proposed again until either concept's class gains or changes a form after the judgment; the session stops when a pass proposes nothing or when the pass number reaches `consolidation.max_passes` in `governance/pipeline-contract.yaml`. Termination does not depend on the bound (section B4); the bound caps effort, as the owner asked ("limited repetitions to ensure exit").

**Confidence.** High (about 85%) that merging by a row with a derived survivor is the right shape for terms: it is the shape the project already uses for every other successor (identity codes, specifications, translations, connections), it leaves every earlier judgment readable as it was made, and it costs one table and one view. Medium (about 65%) on the four proposal reasons being enough: a cross-language duplicate with no seed, no translation and no shared form is not proposed, and only reading finds it (section B6).

## 1. What the rulings require

| Ruling (find it with) | Requirement | Met by |
|---|---|---|
| CLAUDE.md rule 5; OD-18 (`grep -E '^OD-18:' references/project-standards.md`: "status updates on earlier rows allowed, copies of later facts forbidden") | one home per fact; point, do not copy | the merge is one row in base; no row of a later stage is rewritten or copied |
| "retire in place then" (`grep -n -F 'retire in place then' references/project-standards.md | head -3`); OD-29 (`grep -E '^OD-29:' references/project-standards.md`: "both retire in place") | a data row is retired with a reason, never deleted or overwritten | `term_merges` and T-029's rows carry `retired_at`, `retired_by_session`, `retirement_reason` |
| CLAUDE.md rule 8 | derive it, or name who judged it | the survivor and the candidates are derived; each merge and each `distinct` names its judge (session), its time and its reason in named columns |
| O5, O7, O8 of 2026-10-12 (`grep -n -F 'handshake ALL directions' references/project-standards.md`) | centralised, pointers; handshakes in all directions | one resolver view read by every writer and reader; a refusal at every writer that meets a folded id |
| E4 (`grep -n -E '^\| E4 ' references/project-standards.md`) | model-generated aliases are search aids, never vocabulary | a seed may **propose** a pair (reason R3) and never refuses, names or merges anything |
| OD-03 and the T-028 design (`tasks/T-028-design.md`) | a concept is its id; its names are forms in `term_aliases` | the survivor's class is the union of member forms through `v_term_survivor`; no form is moved or copied |
| The 2026-11-06 schema-shape statement (CLAUDE.md §4) | one value per cell; no correction appended to a note | the merge's judge, time and reason are columns, not a dated line in `notes` (the shape `merge-parameter` uses, section A7) |
| CLAUDE.md §8 | the least code that closes the defect | one table, one view, two verbs (`merge-term`, `unmerge-term`), one read verb, one contract key, one kind on T-029's table |

## A. T-129: the merge

### A1. Why a row and a derived survivor, not a re-point (the push `merge-parameter` uses)

- **What `merge-parameter` does** (`grep -n -A30 'def merge_parameter' scripts/db.py`): it sets the folded parameter's `status` and `merged_into`, then UPDATEs `parameter_id` on every row of every table whose foreign key points at `base_parameters`, and appends a dated `MERGED` line to each moved row's `notes`. The moved rows no longer say which parameter their writer named; that fact survives only in prose. It has never been run (`python3 -I -c "import sqlite3;print(sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True).execute(\"select count(*) from base_parameters where status='merged'\").fetchone())"`).
- **Why that shape fails for terms.** The rows that point at a term are (derive: the FK loop of section A5) its forms (`term_aliases`), the adjudications that named it (`term_adjudications`, a judgment-stage record of what an adjudicator said of an observation), the parameter keyed on it (`base_parameters`), a declination (`parameter_declinations`), the searches that used its forms (`search_execution_forms`, through T-026 and T-028's `form_id`), and T-029's relations. Re-pointing an adjudication would make it say the adjudicator named a term it never named; re-pointing a form would make the form's history say it was always a form of the survivor. Both are overwrites of a record (test 2 of the adjudication). A row plus a derived survivor keeps every record as written and makes the merge itself the record.
- **The cost, stated.** Every reader that must see a concept's whole class reads through `v_term_survivor`. Section A5 derives the set of those readers and section A8's red tests hold each.

### A2. The table (sketch; one schema migration, derive its number, never type it)

```
CREATE TABLE term_merges (
  merge_id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  from_term_id        TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES terms(term_id),     -- the folded term
  into_term_id        TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES terms(term_id),     -- its survivor at the time of the merge
  reason              TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(trim(reason)) > 0),
  candidate_reason    TEXT,     -- the proposer's reason code (R1..R4, section B2) that put the pair before the judge, NULL when none did
  created_at          TEXT NOT NULL, created_by_session TEXT NOT NULL,   -- the judge and the time (dbcore.stamp_for)
  retired_at          TEXT, retired_by_session TEXT, retirement_reason TEXT,
  CHECK (from_term_id <> into_term_id),
  CHECK ((retired_at IS NULL AND retired_by_session IS NULL AND retirement_reason IS NULL)
      OR (retired_at IS NOT NULL AND retired_by_session IS NOT NULL AND length(trim(retirement_reason)) > 0))
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ux_term_merges_live_from ON term_merges(from_term_id) WHERE retired_at IS NULL;
```

- `candidate_reason` takes its vocabulary from a CHECK in the same migration (`'R1','R2','R3','R4'`), read by `dbcore.check_values`, so the reason codes have one home and the proposer prints them from there.
- No `notes` column: the judgment is in its own cells.
- `terms` is not altered (no `status`, no `merged_into` on it): whether a term is folded is derived from `term_merges`, so it cannot disagree with it.
- Stage: **base** (the vocabulary layer); Layer 3 rows, Layer 1 schema. `governance/stage-map.yaml` gets `term_merges: base` under `tables:`.

### A3. The view (sketch)

```
CREATE VIEW v_term_survivor AS
WITH RECURSIVE walk(term_id, survivor_id, hops) AS (
  SELECT term_id, term_id, 0 FROM terms
  UNION ALL
  SELECT w.term_id, m.into_term_id, w.hops + 1
    FROM walk w JOIN term_merges m ON m.from_term_id = w.survivor_id AND m.retired_at IS NULL
   WHERE w.hops < (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM terms))          -- a cycle cannot form (A4), and this bounds the walk if one did
SELECT term_id, survivor_id, hops FROM walk w
 WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM term_merges m WHERE m.from_term_id = w.survivor_id AND m.retired_at IS NULL);
```

One row per term: its live survivor (itself when unmerged) and how many merges lie between. It reads base only, so it spans no stage. Python reads it through one helper, `dbcore.term_survivor(conn, term_id)`, which returns the survivor or None for an unknown id; no other code follows `term_merges` itself.

### A4. The verbs

- `db.py merge-term --from TERM-A --into TERM-B --reason TXT [--candidate-reason R1|R2|R3|R4] --session X [--dry-run]`. Refuses, each refusal naming the next action:
  - the same id twice; a blank reason; an unknown id;
  - `--from` already folded (names its survivor: nothing to do, or `unmerge-term` first); `--into` folded (names its survivor: merge into it). So `into` is always live and no cycle can form;
  - **`--from` carries an active parameter** (`base_parameters.status = 'active'` on `--from`): "merge the parameters first with `merge-parameter`, or merge in the other direction". A parameter is keyed on one term; the survivor carries the concept's parameter. When both carry an active parameter, `merge-parameter` is a separate judgment (it moves figures) and runs first;
  - the two disagree on parameter standing: one has a live declination (`parameter_declinations.revoked_at IS NULL`) and the other an active parameter (names `revoke-declination` or `decline-parameter`);
  - a live T-029 row of kind `distinct` between the two (through their survivors): "a judge recorded these as distinct (row N, session S): retire that row with its reason first". A judge changes its mind by a retirement with a reason, never by writing over it;
  - a `candidate_reason` outside the column's CHECK (`dbcore.check_declared`).
  - On success it writes one `term_merges` row and nothing else; it prints the survivor's class size before and after (derived) and every row of every table that points at `--from` (derived by the FK loop of A5) as "now read through the survivor".
- `db.py unmerge-term --merge-id N --reason TXT --session X [--dry-run]`: retires the merge row in place. Refuses a retired row, a blank reason, and an unmerge that would leave a term the survivor of a later merge whose own from-term now resolves elsewhere (derive by re-walking: refuse when `v_term_survivor` would change for any term other than the folded one and its own folded descendants; list them).
- **Every writer that takes a term id resolves it and refuses a folded one, naming the survivor:** `add-alias`, `add-term --distinct-from`, `adjudicate-term --term-id`, `add-parameter`, `decline-parameter`, `rename-term`, `amend-term`, `mint-term-from-catalogue` (its clash screen), T-029's writer, and `request-translation` / `record-translation` when the pointer resolves to a `term_aliases` row of a folded term (it may still be translated: the refusal is only for writing a **new** form or relation to a folded id; a translation of a held form is not refused). Derive the set at execution: `git grep -n -E "term_id|--term-id|--from-term|--distinct-from" -- scripts/db.py` and every parser flag whose value is checked against `terms`.
- **Every name screen reads the survivor's class:** `_name_holder` and `_near_terms` (as T-028 leaves them) report the survivor id, never a folded id, and a near match with a folded term's form is a near match with its survivor.

### A5. The readers (the caller sweep is the design's main cost)

Derive the full set at execution; never use a list typed here as the set:

```
python3 -I -c "import sqlite3;c=sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True);print([(t,f[3]) for (t,) in c.execute(\"select name from sqlite_master where type='table'\") for f in c.execute(f'pragma foreign_key_list(\"{t}\")') if f[2]=='terms'])"
python3 -I -c "import sqlite3;c=sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True);print([n for (n,) in c.execute(\"select name from sqlite_master where type='view' and (sql like '%terms%' or sql like '%term_aliases%' or sql like '%term_id%')\")])"
git grep -n -E "FROM terms|JOIN terms|term_aliases" -- scripts schemas skills .claude ':(exclude)scripts/migrations'
```

A reader is in scope when it answers a question about a **concept** (its names, its forms, its coverage, whether it is a parameter, whether a name is taken). It reads the survivor's class: `JOIN v_term_survivor s ON s.term_id = x.term_id` and groups or filters on `s.survivor_id`. A reader that answers a question about a **record** (what this adjudication named, what this search used) is not changed. Known on 2026-11-17: `v_term_names` (T-028), T-057's base coverage view, the views of A5's second command that print a parameter's name through `terms`, `_name_holder`, `_near_terms`, `scripts/audit/alias_provenance_audit.py`. A view is a caller (CLAUDE.md rule 4): each one rewritten is recreated in the migration, and a view that renders 0 rows on the base is unproven, not clean (exercise it on the fixture of A8).

### A6. `distinct`, on T-029's table

T-029 (amended 2026-11-17) adds the kind `distinct` to its CHECK and retire-in-place columns to its table. **This task** makes `add-term --distinct-from TERM-X` write one `distinct` row per named term, in the same transaction as the term and its adjudication, its warrant the new term's NAMES-NEW adjudication (`term_adjudications.adjudication_id`) and its reason the `--rationale` text, so the judgment that two near names are two concepts is a typed pointer the sweep reads, not a sentence. A `distinct` row is symmetric in meaning; the writer stores it with the lower term id first and refuses a second live row for the same pair.

### A7. What this does not change

- `merge-parameter` keeps its re-point. It moves figures, which the engine gathers by `parameter_id`, and T-059 rewrites that gather. The adjudication registers the difference (`OPEN-ITEMS-PLAN.md` OI-78): when T-059's gather is rewritten, the parameter merge should take this design's shape (a merge row, a survivor view, no re-point, no `MERGED` note line), while no parameter merge has yet been run.
- No trigger is added. The refusal lives in the writers (one home per rule, a refusal that names the next action); a route that bypasses them (a data migration) is caught by the test of A8 run on the rebuilt database and by `term_merge_integrity` below.
- **One read-only integrity check, `scripts/audit/term_merge_integrity.py`**, registered `level: advisory`, `battery: data`, `kinds: [data]`, `basis: unattributed` with `no_floor:` opening `vocabulary-owed —` (no merge exists until a judge makes one): for every live merge, `into` resolves to a live survivor; no live row written **after** the merge's `created_at` (by `created_at`) in a table of A5's first command points at the folded term (a writer that should have refused did not); no live `distinct` row and live merge join the same pair. It prints `EXAMINED: <live merges>`. What reaches the guidebook without it: a form or a parameter filed under a folded term by a route that skipped the writers, so the concept's figures or names split again with nothing red. Ratchet to blocking with `min_items: 1` in the first tooling pull request after T-131 writes the first merge (rule 10: never in T-131's research pull request).

### A8. Red tests (prefix `T129-`; confirm free first: `git grep -c '"T129-' -- scripts/tests` prints nothing)

Test file `scripts/tests/test_term_merges.py`, registered `test_term_merges` (`battery: tests`, `kinds: [tooling, schema]`, `level: advisory`, `basis: hygiene`, `no_floor: selftest — …`). Every probe chosen by query on a scratch copy; fixtures labelled `TASK-FIXTURE`.

| Case | Red before | Green after |
|---|---|---|
| T129-01 | `merge-term` is not a verb | a merge writes one row; `v_term_survivor` maps the folded term to the survivor; no other table's row count or content changes (hash every table but `term_merges` before and after) |

A pair is two distinct **survivors** (`v_term_survivor`). A pair is **judged** when a live row joins its two survivors in `term_merges` (it would no longer be a pair), or in T-029's table (any kind: `distinct`, broader, part of, adjacent, element has parameter, element has provision). A judged pair is proposed again only when the base has grown under the judgment: some member form of either class (or a reviewed translation of one) has `created_at` or `updated_at` later than the judging row's `created_at`. Each pass either judges a proposed pair, which leaves the unjudged set for good (B3: only a later form brings it back, and none is written), or merges two classes, which lowers the number of live survivors by one. The live survivors are finite and only fall; the unjudged pairs among them are finite; so after at most (survivors − 1) merges plus one pass that judges everything left, a pass proposes nothing. The bound exists because the owner asked for limited repetitions, and to cap a batch's effort, not to make the loop end.

Opus-class (the decision is what a phrase names, in its own language). A cross-language duplicate with no attested form in a shared language, no seed in the other's language near the other's attested form, and no reviewed translation. - **A. `merge-parameter`'s re-point for terms.** Overwrites records (A1).

# T-129 design — a merge of two terms is a row, the survivor is derived, and the consolidation sweep proposes, a judge decides, and it ends

_Written 2026-11-17 by an Opus-class adjudicator on the owner's instruction of 2026-11-16 ("have Opus collate all of my questions about this and all of your answers/findings then adjudicate best fixes before planning out how to build followed by folding it into remediation plan"; "ensure compliance with layer architecture, prioritize long-term integrity of project re provenance and consistency"). Plan document: it changes no script, schema, row or ruling. Every count is given as the command that produces it; re-run it. SQL marked **sketch** is a shape, not a file to paste unread. Canadian English. It governs two tasks: section A is T-129 (the merge, NOT FOR SONNET), section B is T-130 (the proposer and its bound, a Sonnet-class executor may run it from this file). The adjudication that chose it is `workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/PROPAGATION-AND-CONSOLIDATION-ADJUDICATION.md`._

## 0. Verdict

**Two terms judged to name one concept are merged by a row, never by rewriting the rows that point at them.** A new base table, `term_merges`, holds one row per merge (the folded term, its survivor, who judged it, when, why) and retires in place when a merge is undone. One view, `v_term_survivor`, follows the live merges to each term's survivor; it is the single home of "which concept is this term now". Rows of every stage that point at the folded term keep pointing at it (they record what their writer said, when it said it); every writer that takes a term id resolves it through the view and refuses a folded term, naming the survivor; every name screen and every reader of a concept's forms reads the survivor's class (its own forms and those of every term folded into it). A judgment that two near-named terms are **not** one concept is a typed row of T-029's term-relation table, kind `distinct`, with its warrant; `add-term --distinct-from` writes it instead of leaving the judgment in the adjudication's free-text rationale.

**The sweep is a read verb, a bound held in the contract, and the batch.** `db.py consolidation-candidates` proposes pairs of live concepts that may be one (four derived reasons, each with the rows that show it); an Opus-class session judges each (merge, relate, distinct, or leave); a judged pair is not proposed again until either concept's class gains or changes a form after the judgment; the session stops when a pass proposes nothing or when the pass number reaches `consolidation.max_passes` in `governance/pipeline-contract.yaml`. Termination does not depend on the bound (section B4); the bound caps effort, as the owner asked ("limited repetitions to ensure exit").

**Confidence.** High (about 85%) that merging by a row with a derived survivor is the right shape for terms: it is the shape the project already uses for every other successor (identity codes, specifications, translations, connections), it leaves every earlier judgment readable as it was made, and it costs one table and one view. Medium (about 65%) on the four proposal reasons being enough: a cross-language duplicate with no seed, no translation and no shared form is not proposed, and only reading finds it (section B6).

## 1. What the rulings require

## A. T-129: the merge

### A1. Why a row and a derived survivor, not a re-point (the push `merge-parameter` uses)

- **What `merge-parameter` does** (`grep -n -A30 'def merge_parameter' scripts/db.py`): it sets the folded parameter's `status` and `merged_into`, then UPDATEs `parameter_id` on every row of every table whose foreign key points at `base_parameters`, and appends a dated `MERGED` line to each moved row's `notes`. The moved rows no longer say which parameter their writer named; that fact survives only in prose. It has never been run (`python3 -I -c "import sqlite3;print(sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True).execute(\"select count(*) from base_parameters where status='merged'\").fetchone())"`).
- **Why that shape fails for terms.** The rows that point at a term are (derive: the FK loop of section A5) its forms (`term_aliases`), the adjudications that named it (`term_adjudications`, a judgment-stage record of what an adjudicator said of an observation), the parameter keyed on it (`base_parameters`), a declination (`parameter_declinations`), the searches that used its forms (`search_execution_forms`, through T-026 and T-028's `form_id`), and T-029's relations. Re-pointing an adjudication would make it say the adjudicator named a term it never named; re-pointing a form would make the form's history say it was always a form of the survivor. Both are overwrites of a record (test 2 of the adjudication). A row plus a derived survivor keeps every record as written and makes the merge itself the record.
- **The cost, stated.** Every reader that must see a concept's whole class reads through `v_term_survivor`. Section A5 derives the set of those readers and section A8's red tests hold each.

### A2. The table (sketch; one schema migration, derive its number, never type it)

```
CREATE TABLE term_merges (
  merge_id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  from_term_id        TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES terms(term_id),     -- the folded term
  into_term_id        TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES terms(term_id),     -- its survivor at the time of the merge
  reason              TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(trim(reason)) > 0),
  candidate_reason    TEXT,     -- the proposer's reason code (R1..R4, section B2) that put the pair before the judge, NULL when none did
  created_at          TEXT NOT NULL, created_by_session TEXT NOT NULL,   -- the judge and the time (dbcore.stamp_for)
  retired_at          TEXT, retired_by_session TEXT, retirement_reason TEXT,
  CHECK (from_term_id <> into_term_id),
  CHECK ((retired_at IS NULL AND retired_by_session IS NULL AND retirement_reason IS NULL)
      OR (retired_at IS NOT NULL AND retired_by_session IS NOT NULL AND length(trim(retirement_reason)) > 0))
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ux_term_merges_live_from ON term_merges(from_term_id) WHERE retired_at IS NULL;
```

- `candidate_reason` takes its vocabulary from a CHECK in the same migration (`'R1','R2','R3','R4'`), read by `dbcore.check_values`, so the reason codes have one home and the proposer prints them from there.
- No `notes` column: the judgment is in its own cells.
- `terms` is not altered (no `status`, no `merged_into` on it): whether a term is folded is derived from `term_merges`, so it cannot disagree with it.
- Stage: **base** (the vocabulary layer); Layer 3 rows, Layer 1 schema. `governance/stage-map.yaml` gets `term_merges: base` under `tables:`.

### A3. The view (sketch)

```
CREATE VIEW v_term_survivor AS
WITH RECURSIVE walk(term_id, survivor_id, hops) AS (
  SELECT term_id, term_id, 0 FROM terms
  UNION ALL
  SELECT w.term_id, m.into_term_id, w.hops + 1
    FROM walk w JOIN term_merges m ON m.from_term_id = w.survivor_id AND m.retired_at IS NULL
   WHERE w.hops < (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM terms))          -- a cycle cannot form (A4), and this bounds the walk if one did
SELECT term_id, survivor_id, hops FROM walk w
 WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM term_merges m WHERE m.from_term_id = w.survivor_id AND m.retired_at IS NULL);
```

1	# T-131  The first consolidation pass over the base: every candidate pair judged, merged, related or kept apart, with its warrant
2	
3	_One task, one pull request (since the owner's instruction of 2026-11-15, one task of a stacked pull request: `grep -n -F "Owner instruction 2026-11-15 — tasks of the remediation plan are stacked" references/project-standards.md`). Read `CLAUDE.md` first; beyond it this file is self-contained. Index, order and the owner decision register: `workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md`. Why this task exists, and the adjudication that chose its shape over the alternatives: `workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/PROPAGATION-AND-CONSOLIDATION-ADJUDICATION.md`. Every number in this file was read on 2026-11-17 and is given with the command that produces it: re-run the command; do not trust the number._
4	
5	**Pilot status.** Not piloted. Authored 2026-11-17 by the Opus-class adjudicator of the owner's propagation and consolidation questions; its evidence command was run read-only on 2026-11-17 and printed what section 3 states. Expect to find a defect in this file, and report it rather than work around it.
6	
7	## 1. Identity
8	
9	| | |
10	|---|---|
11	| Task | T-131 |
12	| Title | The first consolidation pass over the base: every candidate pair judged, merged, related or kept apart, with its warrant |
13	| Wave | research |
14	| Layer (CLAUDE.md §3) | 3 |
15	| Kind | **RESEARCH** (CLAUDE.md rule 10: tooling and research never share a pull request) |
16	| Executor | NOT FOR SONNET: Opus-class. Each verdict is a judgment of what a phrase names, read in its own language |
17	| Traces to | the owner's questions Q2 and Q3 of 2026-11-16; the adjudication `workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/PROPAGATION-AND-CONSOLIDATION-ADJUDICATION.md` (G1); `tasks/T-129-design.md` sections B4 and B5 |
18	
19	## 2. Preconditions
20	
21	- **The integration base.** This workplan must be on the branch you start from. If the workplan's pull request is merged, that is `origin/main`; otherwise the remote branch that carries the newest commit to this folder. Every command in this file uses `$BASE`, set by the first line of the set-up block, and never a literal `origin/main`.
22	- **Tasks that must be merged to the integration base first:** T-130, T-069 merged (T-130 gives the proposer and the bound; T-069 promotes the adjudicated non-English observations to attested forms, which is what gives reasons R1 and R2 something to compare across the held languages). Check by running those tasks' own after-tests (their section 6).
23	- **Owner decisions:** none in the register. A pair either of whose terms has a domain in `dbcore.NON_QUANTITY_DOMAINS` is not merged here: it is listed for the owner in the pull request (design B5).
24	- **Tests that must be red before you start:** `python3 scripts/db.py consolidation-candidates` on the base prints a `CANDIDATES:` line above 0 (if it prints 0, there is nothing to judge: stop and report that, which is a result).
25	- **Set-up.**
26	
27	```
28	cd /home/user/guidebook
29	bash .claude/hooks/ensure-deps.sh && python3 -c "import pydantic, jsonschema, yaml"
30	git fetch origin
31	W=$(git log --remotes --format=%H -1 -- workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline); BASE=$(git branch -r --contains "$W" --format='%(refname:short)' | grep -x origin/main || git branch -r --contains "$W" --format='%(refname:short)' | head -1); echo "BASE=$BASE"
32	git switch -c task/t-131-first-consolidation-pass "$BASE"
33	STEM=session_$(date -u +%Y-%m-%d)-<slug>            # the session stem: bare in the database, with .md for emit_data_migration --session
34	export SCRATCH="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/guidebook-t-131" && mkdir -p "$SCRATCH" && cp data/guidebook.db "$SCRATCH/s.db" && cp data/guidebook.db "$SCRATCH/t.db"   # s.db is the batch's working copy; t.db is for probes
35	```
36	- **Shell variables do not survive from one tool call to the next in this harness.** Write the stem down once and begin every later command block by setting `BASE`, `STEM` and `SCRATCH` again to the same values.
37	- **Real execution:** open with `/session-open`, then `/orient`. Follow `skills/run-pipeline_SKILL.md`. **Pilot or dry run:** skip `/session-open`, stay on the branch you were given, work on the scratch copy only, and stop before the write path.
38	- Work only on the scratch copy, pointing every call at it inline: `GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH="$SCRATCH/s.db" python3 scripts/db.py <verb> ... --session "$STEM"`.
39	- Land the rows only by the write path, after the work is finished:
40	```
41	python3 scripts/research/emit_batch_sql.py --scratch "$SCRATCH/s.db" --out "$SCRATCH/batch.sql"
42	python3 scripts/emit_data_migration.py --session "$STEM.md" --summary "<what the batch is>" --input "$SCRATCH/batch.sql"
43	python3 scripts/migrate_db.py
44	python3 scripts/migrate_db.py --rebuild "$SCRATCH/rebuilt.db"      # must exit 0
45	```
46	Research batches are serial: if another research batch merged after you copied the database, `emit_batch_sql.py` refuses; start again from the new base.
47	
48	## 3. The problem, in the guidebook's terms
49	
50	The base holds concepts that may be one under two names, and forms that two concepts share (T-130's evidence command lists them). Until each pair is judged, a figure may be filed under either, and a determination for one rests on half the evidence while the book prints two topics for one thing. Some shared forms are homonyms (one phrase naming two different quantities in a language): those are recorded as two concepts, not merged.
51	
52	**Evidence command** (read-only):
53	
54	```
55	python3 scripts/db.py consolidation-candidates --pass 1
56	python3 -c "import yaml;print(yaml.safe_load(open('governance/pipeline-contract.yaml'))['consolidation'])"
57	```
58	
59	**Expected output today:** one line per (pair, reason) with its evidence rows, then `EXAMINED:` and `CANDIDATES:` lines (counts computed); the contract's bound.
60	
61	If the output differs, the ground has moved: stop (section 9).
62	
63	## 4. The change
64	
65	1. **Pass by pass, to the bound.** On the scratch copy `$SCRATCH/s.db`: run `consolidation-candidates --pass 1`, judge every line, run `--pass 2`, and so on; stop when a pass prints `CANDIDATES: 0`, or after the pass whose number is the contract's `max_passes` (design B4). Keep each pass's output in `$SCRATCH/pass-<n>.txt`.
66	2. **The verdict for each line** (design B5), each written through `db.py` with `--session "$STEM"`:
67	   - one concept: `merge-term --from <id> --into <id> --reason "<what in the evidence rows shows they are one, in the phrase's own language>" --candidate-reason <R1..R4>`; direction as design B5 says;
68	   - related but not one: T-029's writer, with the kind (broader, part of, adjacent, element has parameter, element has provision) and its warrant;
69	   - two concepts (a homonym, or a near name for another thing): T-029's writer with kind `distinct` and its warrant;
70	   - cannot tell from what is held: leave it; it is listed again and ends in the pull request's list of unjudged pairs, with what would decide it (a form to attest, a translation to review).
71	3. **Never merged here:** a pair marked `owner` by the verb (`NON_QUANTITY_DOMAINS`); a pair whose survivor would carry two active parameters (run `merge-parameter` only if the two parameters are one quantity, which is a judgment you state, and before `merge-term`); never re-point, UPDATE or copy a row.
72	4. Land the rows by the write path of section 2.
73	
74	**What reads what this task writes:** `v_term_survivor` and every concept reader through it (the screens, `v_term_names`, the base coverage view), so the next minting and the next coverage read see one concept; `consolidation-candidates` (a judged pair is not proposed again until the base grows under it); the owner, in the pull request.
75	
76	## 5. Caller sweep
77	
78	A research task renames nothing and changes no code. For each merged pair, search the reading surface for prose that names the folded term as a concept of its own, and correct a sentence your rows make false, or stop if correcting it is not research:
79	
80	```
81	V='<the folded term id or label>'
82	git grep -n -F -e "$V" -- governance architecture CLAUDE.md references skills ':(exclude)references/project-standards.md' ':(exclude)references/search-log'
83	```
84	Structures this task writes: `term_merges`, T-029's relation table. The ledger, `sessions/` and committed migrations are records and are never edited.
85	
86	## 6. Verification
87	
88	**Red before, green after.** Before: section 2's `CANDIDATES:` line is above 0. After (on the migrated database): `python3 scripts/db.py consolidation-candidates` prints `CANDIDATES:` equal to the pairs left unjudged or marked `owner` (derive it from your pass files, never type it), and `python3 scripts/audit/term_merge_integrity.py` passes with `EXAMINED:` equal to the merges this batch wrote: `python3 -I -c "import sqlite3;c=sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True);print(c.execute('select count(*) from term_merges where created_by_session=?',('<STEM>',)).fetchone())"`.
89	
90	**The gates, once each:**
91	```
92	W=$(git log --remotes --format=%H -1 -- workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline); BASE=$(git branch -r --contains "$W" --format='%(refname:short)' | grep -x origin/main || git branch -r --contains "$W" --format='%(refname:short)' | head -1)
93	python3 scripts/audit/research_batch_dod.py --session "$STEM" > "$SCRATCH/dod.txt" 2>&1; echo "rc=$?"; grep -E 'EXAMINED|BLOCKED|PASS|FAIL' "$SCRATCH/dod.txt" | tail -8
94	scripts/preflight.sh --base "$BASE" --explain > "$SCRATCH/gate.txt" 2>&1; echo "rc=$?"; grep -E '^(RESULT|PREFLIGHT|SELFTEST)|FAIL|NOTHING-IN-SCOPE' "$SCRATCH/gate.txt"
95	```
96	Run each once, after the migration is applied and before the commit; never `--all`. `migration_reproducibility` compares row counts only: also run `python3 scripts/audit/migration_reproducibility.py --deep`. A batch that searches and admits nothing is red on `research_dod_session` by construction (OI-55 (1)): report its lines rather than adding a search to satisfy it.
97	
98	## 7. Commit
99	
100	```
101	git add -A . ':!transcripts' ':!*commands.jsonl'
102	git commit -m "run-pipeline: first consolidation pass: candidate pairs judged, merged, related or kept apart [$(date -u '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M')]" -m "<body: every candidate and its verdict, by command output; what was left and why>" -m "<the attribution trailers your own session instructions give>"
103	```
104	
105	## 8. What you must NOT do
106	
107	- Do not write `data/guidebook.db` directly. Rows land only by the write path.
108	- Do not merge a pair marked `owner`; do not judge a pair from its English labels alone when its evidence rows are in another language: read the forms.
109	- Do not mint a term, write a form, a seed or a translation in this batch: the sweep judges what is held (design B4: no form is added within a sweep).
110	- Do not put tooling in this pull request (CLAUDE.md rule 10), and do not change the registry level of `term_merge_integrity` here: its ratchet is the next tooling pull request's.
111	- Do not decide doctrine. Do not treat any `[A-Z]-NN` code as a container. Do not run `run_checks.py --all`, `bootstrap.sh`, or `pip install -r requirements.txt`. Do not push to `main`, rebase or force-push. Do not subscribe to pull-request activity.
112	- Do not hand-type a count into any file or message; write the command that computes it.
113	
114	## 9. Stop conditions
115	
116	Stop and report when: a precondition is not met; the verb's output differs in shape from design B1; a writer refuses a verdict you would have to work around; a pair would need a merge of two active parameters whose quantities you cannot show are one; a pair's evidence is in a language you cannot read with confidence (leave it, listed); you would have to guess a value, a term, a name or an owner's intent.
117	
118	## 10. Rollback
119	
120	Before the migration is applied: delete the scratch copy. After it is committed: a data migration is immutable; undo a wrong merge with `unmerge-term` (its reason stated) and a wrong relation by retiring it, in a compensating batch through the same verbs.
121	
122	## 11. Adversarial pass and pull request
123	
124	Real execution only. `/adversarial` once, recorded with `db.py record-adversarial-pass` and closed with `close-adversarial-pass`; `/batch-done`; push; open the pull request last, once, listing every candidate with its verdict, reason code and evidence rows, the pairs left unjudged with what would decide each, and the pairs marked `owner` as questions for the owner in plain words; call `unsubscribe_pr_activity` at once; push nothing afterwards except a deliberate change. Then, in the next tooling pull request (not this one), ratchet `term_merge_integrity` to blocking with `min_items: 1` (design A7).

# Propagation and consolidation: the owner's four questions, the findings, the adjudication, and the build

_Written 2026-11-17 (UTC) by an Opus-class adjudicator, on the owner's instructions of 2026-11-16, typed in the session `session_2026-11-16-remediation-batch-1-tooling-stack`: (1) "have Opus collate all of my questions about this and all of your answers/findings then adjudicate best fixes before planning out how to build followed by folding it into remediation plan"; (2) "ensure compliance with layer architecture, prioritize long-term integrity of project re provenance and consistency". Planning only: no script, schema, check, migration or database row was changed. Canadian English. Every figure is given as the command that produces it; re-run it, do not trust a number. The input was `scratchpad/session_2026-11-16-remediation-batch-1-tooling-stack/owner-questions-and-findings.md` (gaps G1 to G14) and `.../sweep-list.md`; each claim relied on below was checked against the repository at commit `389c35bb` (`main`), or is marked as resting on the unmerged stacked branch `ccr-cc893571-i4lug4` (`git log --oneline HEAD..origin/ccr-cc893571-i4lug4`)._

**Precedence.** The ledger (`references/project-standards.md`) governs this document (CLAUDE.md rule 0); `TERM-RESOLUTION-PLAN.md` governs it where they conflict (the precedence note of `REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md`). It adds tasks T-129 to T-135, the design `tasks/T-129-design.md`, owner questions OD-68 to OD-70, and open item OI-78; it amends T-028, T-029, T-050, T-110 and T-126 by dated paragraphs.

## 0. Verdict

**The pipeline propagates by pull and refusal, and that is the right pattern; what is missing is the act of consolidation and a few places where a copy stands in for a pointer.** A change reaches the rows that depend on it because they point at it (CLAUDE.md rule 5), because writers refuse until dependents are handled, and because derived lists (the scan ledger, the deferred acts, the coverage views) show what is owed. The owner's question 2 has no answer today: two concepts found to be one cannot be joined (there is no term merge), a judgment that two near names are two concepts is kept only in prose, and nothing proposes candidates after the moment of minting. The best fix is small and keeps every record as it was written: **a merge is a row, the survivor is derived by one view, every writer refuses a folded term naming the survivor, and a read-only proposer offers candidate pairs that an Opus-class judge merges, relates or keeps apart, pass by pass, until a pass proposes nothing or the bound held once in the contract is reached** (T-129, T-130, T-131). The other gaps are owned by existing tasks (G3, G5, G6, G13 in part), settled by convention (G10), declined with reasons (G4, G7's push design, G8's hash extension, G11's cross-stage membership), or are the owner's (G12, G14, and the cross-language clash question the T-028 design left open, now registered).

**Where integrity and minimal code pulled apart, integrity won, and the change was kept small:** a term merge by a row and a derived survivor costs one table and one view more than re-pointing rows as `merge-parameter` does, and in exchange no adjudication, form or search record is ever overwritten (section 3).

## 1. The four questions, verbatim, and what the pipeline does today

### Q1. "how does this pipeline handle identifying new topics for research, conducting them in another language, verifying a source is reputable, adjudicating how much of the source is relevant across different topics, writing down everything relevant including new topics if they don't already exist, judging the parameters for their values as well as assigning their codes as well as assigning evidence tier as well as determining category, and then synthesizing everything within the topic so that it can form a specification/determination?"

| Step the owner names | What does it today (verified) | What is missing |
|---|---|---|
| New topics | Seven stages in `governance/pipeline-contract.yaml` (`python3 -c "import yaml;print([s['id'] for s in yaml.safe_load(open('governance/pipeline-contract.yaml'))['stages']])"`); a concept enters as `db.py observe-term` (verbatim, unjudged), is settled by `adjudicate-term` (outcomes from the column's CHECK: `python3 -I -c "import sys,sqlite3;sys.path.insert(0,'scripts');import dbcore;print(dbcore.check_values(sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True),'term_adjudications','outcome'))"`), then `add-term`, `add-parameter` or `decline-parameter`. The quantity kind and its warrant on `add-parameter` are T-020's, on the stacked branch, not on `main`. | Consolidation after minting (Q2). |
| Another language | A search carries language and jurisdiction; coverage per parameter and bucket member (`lang_jur_map`, `v_coverage_*`); no back-translation (R11). A typed home for translations is T-049's (stacked branch: `git show origin/ccr-cc893571-i4lug4 --stat -- scripts/migrations | grep -i translat`); the renderer's gate for reviewed translations is T-037, not built. | Cross-language concept identity (T-028, open). |
| Reputable source | No "reputable" flag: R10 re-retrieval and the logged retrieval manifest, the author fidelity check, the verification standing `add-source` now requires (T-007, merged), and the tier computed from evidence type and scope (`grep -n 'def derive_tier' schemas/tier_derivation.py`; `adjudication_integrity`, blocking). Type and scope are judged. | The reconciliation of "tier and evidence-type assignment" being "permanently manual" (DR-2026-08-19 §12.5) with a computed tier is unrecorded: OD-70. |
| Relevance across topics | R16: every admission read against the whole parameter list (`record-scan`, `source_scans`, `v_scan_ledger`); relevance is extraction rows per parameter, not a score. | Executing the owed readings (T-105, T-031). |
| Writing down everything, new topics included | `add-extraction`, `observe-term`, the scan ledger's statuses. | — |
| Values, codes, tier | `source_value_extractions`; lens codes on `extraction_lens_links` (three lenses since 2026-11-16: identity, ICF, access need), written by judgment, the maps only proposing (MAPPING-DESIGN; T-126, open); tier as above. | T-126, T-127, T-128 (OD-67). |
| "Determining category" | Not one field. Five candidates hold: evidence type (judged) and tier (computed); claim type (`claim_type`); a concept's topic domain (`terms.domain`); quantity kind (T-020); design scale (`specifications.design_scale`). **Found here:** `terms.domain` has no CHECK (`grep -n -F 'has no CHECK, so there is no vocabulary' scripts/db.py`), `amend-term` accepts a domain only if a live row already carries it, and the non-quantity domains are a typed list in code (`grep -n '^NON_QUANTITY_DOMAINS' scripts/dbcore.py`). | Which the owner meant: OD-69. |
| Synthesis and determination | `convergence_assessment` (Opus-only); `specifications` keyed on parameter plus at least one lens column, computed by the engine (`grep -n '^RULE_VERSION' scripts/assess/assess_cell.py`), never hand-assigned (owner, 2026-09-09 evening). No determination is live: `python3 -I -c "import sqlite3;print(sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True).execute('select count(*), sum(retired_at is null) from specifications').fetchone())"`. | T-059, T-068, T-124, T-110. |

### Q2. "is there an iterative loop with limited repetitions to ensure exit such that you can ensure that topics across languages and synonyms are properly consolidated and associated in base with those consolidations propagating forward throughout database so we don't end up with duplicates or near identical topics?"

**Today: no.** Verified: a write-time near-duplicate refusal (`grep -n -A30 'def _near_terms' scripts/db.py`: token-set subset or superset against every label and every alias whose `attestation` is not `model_seed`, in any language; refused unless `--distinct-from` with a rationale); exact clashes (`_name_holder`); adjudication NAMES-EXISTING; `merge-parameter`, `rename-term`, `retire-parameter`. **There is no verb that merges two terms** (`python3 scripts/db.py --help | tr ',{}' '\n\n\n' | grep -c -x -E 'merge-term|retire-term'` prints 0; G2 is confirmed, every parser read, not only the names). Bounded iteration exists only for citation mining (depth 1, `grep -n 'Depth-1 enforced' skills/citation-miner_SKILL.md`) and a recorded `saturation_signal` on `search_executions`.

**What the findings did not say, found here.** (a) Forms are already shared by two concepts in one language: `python3 -I -c "import sqlite3;print(sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True).execute(\"select upper(language), lower(alias), group_concat(distinct term_id), group_concat(distinct attestation) from term_aliases where alias_type not in ('NARROWER','BROADER') group by 1,2 having count(distinct term_id)>1\").fetchall())"`. Some are seeds; some are unrecorded aliases; at least one is a homonym (the Spanish "paso libre" is held by both the corridor-width and the door-width concepts), which a judge records as two concepts rather than merges. (b) `add-term --distinct-from` keeps the judgment that two near names are two concepts only inside the new term's adjudication `rationale` (`grep -n -B2 -A12 'near = \[(t, h) for t, h in _near_terms' scripts/db.py`), so no later pass can know the pair was judged. (c) T-029's file names "a merge (`merge-parameter`, `rename-term`)" as the act for two terms that name one concept (`grep -n -F 'the act is a merge' workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/tasks/T-029-term-relations.md`); neither verb merges terms. (d) `merge-parameter` re-points every row that holds the folded id (UPDATE) and records the move as a dated `MERGED` line appended to each moved row's `notes`, the shape the 2026-11-06 schema-shape statement forbids ("a correction appended to a note"); it has never been run (`python3 -I -c "import sqlite3;print(sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True).execute(\"select count(*) from base_parameters where status='merged'\").fetchone())"`).

### Q3. "you have identified missing items. what else exists in pipeline that allows us to work in all directions and systematically perform new passes over already-recorsed rows to ensure that the database codes/terms/etc are consistently applied as well as to append existing rows with more information as required if the base gets extended?"

**Today: owed passes are derived and listed; they are run by research batches; there is no scheduler and none is wanted.** Verified: `v_scan_ledger`, `v_reading_owed`, `v_deferred_acts` (T-079, merged: a deferral stands while its cell is owed, and follows `merged_into`), `scan_debt` (advisory, red whenever debt exists, no baseline by design), `verified_scan_integrity` (advisory, red on extractions with no recorded reading), the `v_coverage_*` views, `unmined`, `unmined-gaps`, `cell-status`, `coverage`, and the COVERAGE reads of `/batch-done` (T-090, merged; `grep -n '## COVERAGE' .claude/commands/batch-done.md`). Appending to a recorded figure is by new pointer rows (`add-lens-link`, `retire-lens-link`, `add-population-icf-link`, `retire-identity` with a successor), retire-in-place (specifications; admission edges and connections once T-050 merges) and narrow `amend-*` verbs. **One re-pass per kind of base extension**, which is the answer to the question:

| The base grows by | The rows that may now owe more | Derived by | Executed by |
|---|---|---|---|
| a parameter | every held source × the new parameter | `v_scan_ledger`, `scan_debt`; T-031's clause inventory and re-read flag | T-105 and every batch (R16) |
| a lens code or map row | figures recorded before the base could propose a group | T-126's audit lists (i) and, by this adjudication's amendment, (iii) | T-127, T-106 and their successors |
| a form, a seed or a translation | pairs of concepts that may be one | T-130's `consolidation-candidates` (new) | T-131 and every later batch, through `/batch-done` |
| a language-jurisdiction pair | concepts with no form there | T-057's base coverage view; `v_research_scope` | T-107 |
| a source's verification or tier, a grading, an edge | a stored determination | `derivation_handshake_integrity` (recompute) | retire and re-determine; blocking once T-132 lands |

### Q4. "in fact, how does the pipeline handle propagation in all directions whenever there is a change made to a row or a new row somewhere is made?"

**By pull and by refusal, not by push.** Verified: the schema holds one trigger (`python3 -I -c "import sqlite3;print(sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True).execute(\"select name from sqlite_master where type='trigger'\").fetchall())"`); a change reaches dependents because they point at the row (the views: `python3 -I -c "import sqlite3;print(sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True).execute(\"select count(*) from sqlite_master where type='view'\").fetchone())"`; the findings' figure is the stacked branch's, which adds `v_translations_current`); through a cascade held in one place (`merge-parameter`, successor columns, `merged_into` followed by `v_deferred_acts`); through writers that refuse until dependents are handled (merge and retire refuse a live determination and an open gate); through determinations as recomputable caches (`derivation_sha` hashes the graded link set, each figure's in-lens state and the three lens codes; `derivation_handshake_integrity` recomputes the rest); through the capture path (scratch copy, `dbcore.writable_tables`, `emit_batch_sql.py`, migration only) and the replay checks; and through read-only audits. **Corrected here:** the findings (G7) name "the verification cron" as a route that bypasses the writers; it was deleted on 2026-10-14 (`grep -n -F 'The scheduled cron that polled this pool was deleted' scripts/audit/research_batch_dod.py`). Three sentences still name it as live (`grep -n -i cron scripts/audit/derivation_handshake_integrity.py scripts/assess/assess_cell.py governance/research-contract.yaml`): prose callers, repaired by T-132.

## 2. The adjudication, gap by gap

Order of preference for every fix (CLAUDE.md §8): do nothing and say why; change a rule or convention; reuse what exists; delete the cause; only then the smallest code. Tests in priority: (1) layer compliance, (2) long-term provenance, (3) long-term consistency, (4) minimal code.

| Gap | Decision | The fix, in one line | Why this and not another |
|---|---|---|---|
| **G1** no bounded consolidation sweep | **NEW: T-130 (tooling), T-131 (research)**, on T-129 | a read verb proposes candidate pairs for four derived reasons; an Opus judge merges, relates or keeps apart; stop when a pass proposes nothing or at `consolidation.max_passes` (3) in the contract | the candidates, the bound and the record of who judged are each held once (data, the contract, the judging rows); a stored candidate list or a pass counter would be a second home of derivable facts (rule 8); a check red while candidates exist would be red by construction (rule 6), so the list is printed by `/batch-done` |
| **G2** no `merge-term` | **NEW: T-129** (design `tasks/T-129-design.md` §A) | a merge is a `term_merges` row (judge, time, reason, retire-in-place), `v_term_survivor` derives each term's survivor, every writer refuses a folded term naming the survivor, every concept reader reads the survivor's class; `add-term --distinct-from` writes a T-029 `distinct` row | test 2: a re-point would overwrite adjudications and forms (the records of what was said); a row plus a derived survivor keeps them, as `retire-identity`, `specifications` and `translations` already do |
| **G3** no cross-language concept identity | **OWNED** by T-028 (concept id, forms per occurrence), T-057 (base coverage per concept and pair), T-069 and T-107 (forms), T-049 and T-112 (translations); **T-028 amended** (OD-68 registered; one function for the near rule) | nothing new beyond T-129 and T-130, which give the identity its merge and its proposals | the open question in T-028's design, whether an identical string in two languages for two concepts is a clash, is the owner's: OD-68 |
| **G4** the near screen skips `model_seed` aliases | **DECLINED** as a defect; the cross-language catch moves to T-130's reason R3 | seeds **propose** pairs; they never refuse, name or merge | E4 (`grep -n -E '^\| E4 ' references/project-standards.md`): a seed is a search aid, never vocabulary; a seed that refused a name would let a model's guess block an observed phrase. **Correction to the finding:** the screen does compare `unrecorded` aliases in every language, but a token-set screen almost never matches across scripts and languages, so in practice it catches a cross-language duplicate only where a same-language form exists |
| **G5** owed passes listed, not executed | **OWNED** by T-031 (clause inventory, derived re-read flag), T-105 (read what is held), T-062 (a verified figure with no reading refused at rest); T-079 and T-090 merged | do nothing more; **DECLINED:** a scheduler | the batch is the loop and `/batch-done` is the cue; each owed pair exits by a reading, a deferral with its reason and age (`v_deferred_acts`), or the derived re-read flag; a scheduler is apparatus whose only reader would be itself (§8). `scan_debt` and `verified_scan_integrity` red is research debt, not a tooling defect |

The cheapest reliable detector already exists; it only has to bind |
| **G9** tolerated second homes | **NEW: T-133** | `v_open_determination_gates` reads a gate's tier and type through `trigger_ref_id`; `specification_map_links` points at the `identity_icf_map` rows the function path read; `functional_basis` NULL forward; parity items 4 and 5 deleted | rule 5: "a parity check is not a fix"; map rows retire in place, so a pointer keeps the history the copy kept; no determination is live, so it is cheapest now (T-110 waits for it). **Correction:** `governing_refs` is not a live second home: it was writer-retired on 2026-09-21 (`grep -n 'WRITER-RETIRE (2026-09-21)' scripts/assess/assess_cell.py`) |

## 4. Pull against push, and the drift detector

**The project's pattern is enough, with one addition.** Pull (rows point; readers derive) and refuse (writers stop a write that would leave a dependent wrong, and name the next action) keep one home per rule and leave every record as written. Push by triggers would duplicate the writers' rules in SQL, hide them from the refusal register, and rewrite rows of later stages from earlier ones. The addition is the **merge as a row with a derived survivor**, which turns the one place the project lacked a pull mechanism (two concepts becoming one) into the same pattern. **The cheapest reliable drift detector is the recompute**, not a longer hash: it is the engine itself, so it cannot disagree with the engine about what the inputs are; it needs only to bind, which T-132 does once a determination is live.
